title: From SDET to AI quality engineer
text: Track A uses AI to improve software testing: generating API test candidates, classifying CI failures, or proposing missing edge cases. The generated artifacts still need review and deterministic execution. Track B tests the AI application itself: whether a chatbot stays grounded, whether retrieval finds the right document, and whether an agent calls an authorized tool. Treat its output as evidence to evaluate, not a trustworthy oracle.  A REST endpoint may promise an exact status code and schema. A chatbot can express the same correct answer in many ways. Separate hard invariants (valid JSON, no forbidden tool, citation points to supplied evidence) from quality rubrics (helpfulness, completeness, groundedness). Freeze representative test inputs and application versions. Run repeated samples when variation matters. Record outputs, scores, cost, latency, and failure categories. One passing response is not proof of reliability.  Build Python, data, SQL, and statistical foundations before abstractions. Then learn embeddings and retrieval before RAG frameworks; tool calling before agents; evaluation before release. An AI engineer assembles useful model-powered systems. An ML engineer develops model training and serving pipelines. A data scientist investigates data and experiments. An AI quality engineer designs evidence and controls across those systems. Roles overlap; judge work by its purpose.

title: A reproducible engineering workspace
text:
Use a project-specific virtual environment. Select its interpreter in VS Code. Keep dependency declarations in the repository and record the Python version in your README. A package imported from your global machine can hide a missing dependency. A notebook is useful for inspecting data and plots. Move durable logic into importable modules with tests. Git should track source and small synthetic datasets, not virtual environments or secret files. python -m venv .venv
# Linux / macOS
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest The course executes educational Python and SQL in your browser. It has no provider key and no model API requirement. Optional local labs use a Python process on your machine. A browser bundle is downloadable by every visitor. An environment variable prefixed for Vite client use is still public after bundling. Keep provider credentials exclusively in local processes or a properly authenticated server. import os
api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
# Never print api_key or commit a populated .env file. A notebook is useful for inspecting one experiment, but execution order can hide dependencies: a cell may succeed only because an earlier cell created a variable. Move the analyzer into an importable function and run it from a fresh interpreter. Keep a small notebook as a consumer of that function rather than a second implementation. Use a virtual environment per project and install from a reviewed manifest. Record Python and package versions with the run artifact; a requirements range alone does not recreate a particular installation. Store a tested lock or freeze after validation. Verify setup with an import smoke test and the analyzer's behavior tests before connecting a provider. A key belongs in the local process environment and must be excluded from Git, browser bundles and progress backups.

title: Define an AI release contract
Phase 00 checkpoint: apply, break and evaluate
Values, collections, and API contracts
text:
Names bind to objects; they are not storage boxes with fixed types. Integers, floats, strings, booleans, and None represent distinct meanings. The string "false" is truthy because it is non-empty. Never convert an API flag with bool(raw) when raw might be a string. Lists preserve order and allow mutation; tuples represent fixed ordered records; dictionaries map keys to values; sets store unique hashable values. Choose a set for duplicate test IDs and a list for ordered execution results. result = {"name": "login", "status": "failed", "duration": 4.5}
failed_ids = {"login", "checkout", "login"}
print(len(failed_ids))  # 2
print(result.get("retries", 0))  # 0 Assigning a list to another name does not copy it. Mutating through either name changes the same object. A shallow copy only copies the outer collection; nested dictionaries still share identity. Use direct indexing for a required field when absence is an error. Use .get for optional values only when a default has a defined meaning. Validate status values before computing pass rate; silently treating unknown status as pass corrupts metrics. original = [{"status": "failed"}]
copy = original.copy()
copy[0]["status"] = "passed"
print(original[0]["status"])  # passed A dictionary maps stable test IDs to records; a set records membership such as already-seen IDs; a list preserves an ordered event stream. Choosing a set for the event stream discards ordering and duplicates, which can hide repeated failures. A tuple can represent a fixed composite identity such as tenant, build and test. Mutability matters when fixtures are shared. Assigning second = first does not copy a list, and a shallow dictionary copy still shares nested lists. A test that appends to a nested fixture can change later tests. Build a fresh fixture for each test or copy the exact mutable boundary. Test duplicates, absent keys and unexpected field types, and avoid using a mutable default argument such as failures=[] in a function signature.

title: Filter, transform, and summarize test runs
text:
An if statement branches by a condition. A for loop iterates over objects directly. A comprehension expresses a simple filter and transformation together; keep complex business decisions in a named function. A function should have an explicit contract: inputs, output shape, and exceptional cases. Parameters are local names. return sends a value to the caller; print only writes a display message. runs = [{"name": "login", "status": "failed"},
        {"name": "search", "status": "passed"}]
failed = [r["name"] for r in runs if r["status"] == "failed"]
print(failed) A pass rate for no test executions is undefined; return None or raise a domain error rather than claiming 100%. Use type hints to communicate that possibility. Avoid hidden globals and mutable default arguments. A default list is created once when the function is defined, so repeated calls can unintentionally share state. Use None and create a new list inside the function. def pass_rate(runs):
    if not runs:
        return None
    return sum(r["status"] == "passed" for r in runs) / len(runs) A comprehension is a transformation, not a substitute for readable error handling. Collect failed records with a clear predicate, then compute summaries separately. If a status is missing, decide explicitly whether to reject the record or label it unknown; silently treating it as passed changes the denominator. Short-circuit operators return operands, which can be useful but surprising: value or default replaces valid falsy values such as zero. A zero duration is different from a missing duration. Use is None when absence is the intended condition. Test an empty run list, all passes, all failures, missing fields and zero durations. These cases establish the analyzer's contract independently of the large synthetic dataset.

title: Functions, arguments, and maintainable modules
Types, validation, and error boundaries
Test the analyzer, including what can break
Bounded async, cancellation, and retry
text:
Async functions suspend at await so other tasks can progress during I/O. They do not turn CPU-heavy parsing into parallel computation. Blocking a model SDK or file transform inside an async route can still stall every concurrent request. Concurrency should be a budget: use a semaphore to bound outstanding API calls and define a deadline for the whole operation. A generator yields records lazily; an async generator can stream observations without retaining an entire report.  Use async with for locks and resource lifetimes. asyncio.wait_for bounds a coroutine and cancels it on timeout; propagate cancellation rather than catching it as an ordinary successful result. Retry only classified transient errors within the original deadline. Decorators can add timing while functools.wraps preserves names and metadata. Keep retry/timing wrappers separate from business transformation. Test both the returned values and whether cancellation closes the underlying resource. import asyncio
async def collect(items, fetch, limit=2):
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)
    async def one(item):
        async with sem:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(fetch(item), 2)
    return await asyncio.gather(*(one(x) for x in items)) Unbounded gather over thousands of CI logs can exhaust sockets and trigger rate limits. A synchronous sleep in an async retry blocks the event loop; use asyncio.sleep. Repeated retries with a fresh timeout can exceed the user’s overall request budget. Inject a fake clock or zero delay and a fake transport for tests. Count attempts, assert a permanent error is not retried, and check cancellation leaves no background write. Do not retry a non-idempotent action without an idempotency contract.  Exercise a bounded fetcher with slow, successful, transient, and permanent responses. Measure maximum simultaneous calls, total deadline, and abandoned work. Testing concurrency is about observable contracts rather than an exact scheduler order. This applies to Playwright API checks, batched log analysis, provider requests, and future agent tools. A good interview explanation names the independent I/O work and the enforced concurrency budget.

title: Classes, enums, Pydantic, and contract testing
text:
Classes group state and behavior; a dataclass is convenient for an internal record, and an enum restricts named domain choices. Inheritance can model a stable substitutable interface, but composition is usually clearer for a transport, validator, and reporter. Static types assist review and tools. External JSON still needs runtime validation. Pydantic models can enforce bounds and forbid extra fields; strict behavior must be selected deliberately because coercion can otherwise accept a string where a number was intended.  Create a request model with a bounded log, explicit category enum, and strict duration. Use model_validate at the API boundary and model_dump for serialization. Use field validators for rules that involve more than basic types. In tests, parameterize valid and invalid requests. A fixture constructs a new service per test; monkeypatch replaces environment values without leaking them to the next test. Mock an adapter protocol so schema validation and business logic remain real. from enum import Enum
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class Status(str, Enum):
    passed="passed"
    failed="failed"
class Result(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    name: str = Field(min_length=1)
    status: Status
    duration: float = Field(ge=0, strict=True) A unit mock that returns prevalidated domain objects bypasses the dangerous parsing boundary. Include integration cases with missing keys, extra keys, negative values, booleans in numeric fields, and invalid enums. Property tests verify invariants over generated records. A marker can separate network integration tests, but excluding all of them forever is not a quality strategy. Know which tests ran, and retain one meaningful adapter contract check with synthetic payloads.  Keep request, response, and internal state models distinct so a response cannot leak private transport fields. Test serialization and exception mapping as part of the public API contract. Demonstrate a fixture’s cleanup with a failing test. This pattern transfers directly to REST/GraphQL contract testing and structured AI output. A valid schema is necessary, but it cannot establish that a predicted defect category is factually correct.

title: Files, structured logs, and streaming reports
text:
pathlib makes path composition explicit across operating systems. JSON preserves nested records; CSV represents rows and needs a defined dialect, schema, and encoding. Environment variables configure processes without committing secrets. A context manager owns cleanup even when parsing fails. Iterators and generators let a result analyzer process large histories incrementally, but consumers must understand that a stream is exhausted after iteration.  Separate reading from transformation and writing. Open files with encoding=utf-8 and newline="" for CSV. Validate rows as they are read and retain rejected-row counts. Emit JSON logs containing event, run_id, stage, and outcome; redact log bodies and credentials. Write reports atomically: create a temporary sibling file, flush it, then replace the final path. A crash should leave either the previous complete report or the new one, rather than a partially written artifact. import csv
from pathlib import Path
def rows(path):
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        yield from csv.DictReader(stream)
# list(rows("datasets/test-runs.csv")) A relative path can refer to a different directory in CI than in VS Code. Anchor fixture paths to the repository or require an explicit CLI argument. Logging the entire environment can expose provider credentials. A reused generator can produce an empty second metric pass. Aggregate in one pass or deliberately materialize bounded input. Test a corrupt row halfway through a stream and verify cleanup and error reporting.  Build a CLI report containing accepted rows, rejected rows, failure frequency, and duration summaries. Make exit status nonzero for violated ingestion policy so GitHub Actions can block the pipeline. Keep ordinary empty input distinguishable from a failed read. The same boundaries support dataset ingestion, evaluation artifacts, and incident reports. An SDET should be able to reproduce an artifact from a clean checkout and explain every excluded record.

title: Arrays, shapes, and vectorized metrics
text:
A NumPy ndarray stores typed values in a multidimensional shape. A matrix shaped (runs, tests) has one row per run. sum(axis=0) reduces the run axis and produces one value per test. sum(axis=1) produces one value per run. Vectorized operations apply across arrays efficiently. A boolean mask selects observations. Slices can share memory with the original array, so use .copy() when mutation should be isolated. import numpy as np
passed = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
print(passed.shape)  # (2, 3)
print(passed.mean(axis=0))  # rate for each test NumPy compares trailing dimensions. Dimensions match when equal or when one is 1. An array of shape (3,) can be added to (2, 3); an array of shape (2,) cannot without reshaping to (2, 1). The result may be valid mathematically but wrong semantically. Label axes before operations. Explicitly choose floating-point dtype before division or normalization; integer storage can truncate derived values. latency = np.array([[100., 200., 300.], [120., 220., 330.]])
baseline = np.array([100., 200., 300.])
print(latency / baseline) For a duration table shaped [builds, tests], axis=0 aggregates across builds and axis=1 aggregates across tests. Keep axis names in comments or variable names because an array does not retain the meaning of its coordinates automatically. A scalar, row vector and column vector have different broadcasting behavior. Boolean masks select elements satisfying a condition; using a mask with the wrong shape can fail or select the wrong subset. Check dtype and finite values before computing statistics. Integer arrays are appropriate for IDs but floating-point arrays are needed for normalized metrics. Test a one-row table, a one-column table, empty arrays and NaN values. Compare vectorized output with a small explicit loop as an independent oracle.

title: Cosine similarity from first principles
text:
A vector is an ordered list of numeric coordinates. An embedding model learns representations whose geometry can capture useful relationships. The synthetic vectors in this lab are hand-designed for arithmetic practice; they are not real semantic embeddings. The dot product sums pairwise coordinate products. A norm measures length. Cosine similarity divides the dot product by both lengths, so it compares direction. Cosine 1 means the same direction; 0 is orthogonal; -1 is opposite. import numpy as np
a = np.array([1., 2., 0.])
b = np.array([2., 4., 0.])
print(np.dot(a, b))  # 10
print(np.linalg.norm(a))  # sqrt(5) A unit vector is v / norm(v). For unit vectors the dot product equals cosine similarity. Squared Euclidean distance between unit vectors is 2 - 2*cosine, so they induce the same ranking. Unnormalized dot product also rewards magnitude. A zero vector has no direction, so cosine is undefined. Reject it or apply a documented fallback. Do not divide by zero and hope NaN sorting will produce sensible retrieval results.  Raw dot product rewards magnitude as well as direction. For a=[1,0], b=[10,1] and c=[1,0], b has a larger dot product than c but lower cosine similarity. This difference matters when an index is configured for dot distance while embeddings are not normalized. A zero vector has no direction. The teaching implementation returns a declared zero score, while another application may reject it; either policy must be explicit and tested. Reject mismatched dimensions rather than letting zip silently truncate coordinates. In retrieval, keep document identity aligned with vector rows, and test identical, opposite, orthogonal and zero vectors. Geometric similarity remains evidence for ranking, not proof that two failure causes are the same.

title: Sampling, masks, and reproducible experiments
text:
Use np.random.default_rng(seed) and keep the seed with the experiment. A fixed seed helps reproduce one sample but does not prove stability across samples. Sample multiple seeds when estimating uncertainty. A mask such as durations > 5 identifies slow observations; np.percentile returns a tail summary. The mean can hide a small group of severe outliers, so retain raw observations and relevant segments. import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
durations = rng.lognormal(mean=1, sigma=0.5, size=100)
print(np.percentile(durations, 95))
print(durations[durations > 5].size) Sampling only successful production interactions creates survivorship bias. Include unsuccessful requests, rare categories, long inputs, empty retrieval, and adversarial inputs in separately labeled slices. Keep training, tuning, and final evaluation samples separate. Changing a prompt repeatedly against the final evaluation set effectively trains your decisions on that set.  A random seed reproduces a pseudo-random sequence under a fixed implementation and data order; it does not make a sample representative. Uniform row sampling can underrepresent rare product defects or repeat many rows from one incident. Stratification preserves selected class proportions, while group sampling avoids splitting closely related incidents across partitions. Report which sampling unit was used: run, test, incident or build. For uncertainty estimates over correlated runs, resample independent incidents rather than individual repeated observations. Keep a sealed holdout that was not inspected during iteration. Test that sampled IDs are valid, groups are disjoint where required and every necessary class has coverage. Reproducibility and representativeness are separate evaluation properties.

title: Matrix shapes and normalized batch similarity
text:
Embedding search can score many documents at once with a matrix product. If queries have shape [q,d] and documents [n,d], normalize each row and multiply queries by documents transposed to obtain [q,n]. Each output row is one query's score against every document. The shared dimension d is a contract, not a value that can be reshaped arbitrarily. A transpose changes axes; reshape reorganizes the same flat storage. Confusing them can return the right dimensions with the wrong numerical relationships.  Compute row norms with axis=1 and keepdims=True, then divide using a zero-safe output. This broadcasts one norm per row across its d coordinates. Matrix multiplication @ performs a dot product along the shared dimension; elementwise * does not aggregate. For queries [[1,0],[0,1]] and documents [[1,0],[1,1]], normalized scores are [[1,.707],[0,.707]]. Test against the manual cosine calculation before trusting a large batch. Keep dtype and finite-value checks at the boundary. import numpy as np
q=np.array([[1.,0.],[0.,1.]])
d=np.array([[1.,0.],[1.,1.]])
d=d/np.linalg.norm(d,axis=1,keepdims=True)
print(q@d.T) Normalizing the whole matrix by one global norm changes ranking assumptions. Dividing integer arrays in place can fail or truncate under an inappropriate dtype. An empty document collection requires a correctly shaped empty score matrix, not an index error. Check dimension mismatch, zero rows, non-finite values and each result's query/document identity. Use small hand-computed matrices as an independent oracle.  Vectorized scoring is useful for transparent exact-retrieval reference results. Measure its runtime separately from embedding generation and compare numerical results with the single-vector implementation. For SDETs, shapes and mathematical invariants are powerful tests: normalized nonzero rows have norm one, self-similarity is one and orthogonal similarity is zero. They can detect wrong axes without requiring a large model or provider account.

title: Clean test history without hiding defects
text:
A DataFrame is a labeled table; each column is a Series. Start with head(), info(), dtypes, and isna().sum(). Read CSV with explicit types when identifiers have leading zeros. Parse timestamps with a defined timezone. Selecting df["duration"] gives a Series; df[["duration"]] gives a DataFrame. Use .loc for explicit row and column selection. Copy a filtered slice before modifying it when isolation is required. import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"test": "login", "build": 1, "status": "failed", "duration": 4.5},
    {"test": "login", "build": 2, "status": "passed", "duration": None},
])
print(df.isna().sum())
print(df.loc[df["status"] == "failed", ["test", "build"]]) A missing duration should remain unknown for latency analysis, not become zero. A missing status should be quarantined or counted separately. Preserve the denominator used in every metric. Deduplicate by the ingestion identity, not merely by test name. Two executions of the same test in one build can be intentional retries. A stable key might include build_id, test_id, attempt, and environment. Keep raw data and document every cleaning decision.  Missing data needs a domain interpretation before imputation. A missing duration may indicate a cancelled test; filling it with zero can make an outage look like a performance improvement. Preserve a missingness indicator and distinguish not-run from passed. Stable test IDs are safer join keys than display names that may be renamed. Check duplicates on the intended identity, such as tenant, build and test, rather than dropping identical rows indiscriminately. A legitimate rerun has a different run ID and may be required to measure flakiness. Preserve raw records, clean in a reproducible function and count rejected or changed rows. Test malformed durations, duplicate identities and missing statuses, and verify that cleaning does not silently change the total population used for pass-rate metrics.

title: Pass rates and flaky-test analysis
text:
Create a passed indicator and take its mean within each test group. This measures run-level pass rate. A test-level report answers a different question: how many distinct tests exhibit a behavior? Name the denominator in your report. A mixed-outcome test has at least one pass and one fail in the observation window. Different code versions, environments, or test data can explain that pattern. Analyze repeated runs under comparable conditions before asserting nondeterministic flakiness. import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({"test": ["login", "login", "search"],
                   "status": ["failed", "passed", "passed"]})
df["passed"] = df["status"].eq("passed")
print(df.groupby("test")["passed"].mean()) Aggregate counts, median duration, and p95 by module and build. Retain failed-first-attempt rate separately from eventual pass rate so retries cannot hide instability. Sort by impact, not merely count: consider failure frequency, business criticality, added retry time, and reproducibility. Use pivot tables for build-by-module summaries and convert timestamps before resampling.  A per-module pass rate needs the correct denominator. Excluding cancelled or missing-status rows may be a defensible policy, but report that exclusion; otherwise a module with many unexecuted tests can appear healthy. Weighted overall pass rate differs from the mean of module rates when modules have different numbers of runs. Flakiness is not simply any test that ever failed. A candidate may show mixed pass/fail outcomes under comparable builds, but environment changes and product fixes can also explain the variation. Group by stable test identity, order by time and retain build context. Test all-pass, all-fail, mixed outcomes and one-run tests. Label the result a flaky-test candidate until the controlled reproduction establishes nondeterministic behavior.

title: Joins, time windows, and regression signals
text:
Join executions to test metadata by stable test_id. validate="many_to_one" asserts that each metadata key appears once. A many-to-many join multiplies matching rows and inflates counts; inspect unmatched keys with indicator=True. Use a left join to retain unknown tests for investigation. An inner join silently removes records with missing metadata. Group by environment and build when comparing performance. # runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", how="left",
#            validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
import pandas as pd
runs = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,1,2], "duration": [2.,3.,1.]})
cases = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,2], "module": ["auth","search"]})
print(runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", validate="many_to_one")) Sort within a test by timestamp before shift() or rolling(). Use lagged features when predicting a future failure; a rolling window that includes the outcome leaks future information. For a latency trend, compare median and tail within stable workloads and report sample sizes. A different mix of tests can change overall mean even when each test has unchanged latency.  A many-to-many join multiplies rows. If a test appears twice in both tables, the joined result contains four combinations; a later mean or count can be wrong even though no exception occurred. Use validate='many_to_one' when enriching runs with a single testcase record, and inspect unmatched keys with an indicator column. Parse timestamps with an explicit timezone and sort within the test group before calculating lagged duration features. Input row order is not a chronological guarantee. A future build's duration must not become a feature for an earlier prediction. Test duplicate enrichment keys, unmatched IDs, tied timestamps and timezone conversion. Compare row counts before and after the join and retain the reason for every intended change.

title: Pivot tables, UTC time, and leakage-safe features
text:
A pivot table turns row observations into a labeled matrix after aggregation. Choose index, columns, values, and aggregation explicitly: module-by-build first-attempt failure rate differs from test-by-date mean duration. Missing cells mean no observation, not zero failures. Parse timestamps to timezone-aware UTC before sorting or resampling. Daylight-saving changes and mixed local offsets can create ambiguous ordering. Keep categorical identifiers as categories only when their vocabulary and unknown-value policy are defined.  Use pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True), sort by test and timestamp, then group and shift to build lagged features. Merge metadata with validate="many_to_one". A rolling feature for prediction must use observations strictly before the predicted run. Prefer vectorized transforms and map for straightforward substitutions; apply is useful for complex row logic but can be slower and conceal type changes. Inspect dtypes after transformations and keep raw evidence immutable. import pandas as pd
df=pd.DataFrame({"test":["a","a","b"],"duration":[2.,4.,1.],"build":[1,2,1]})
print(df.pivot_table(index="test",columns="build",values="duration",aggfunc="mean"))
print(df.sort_values(["test","build"]).groupby("test")["duration"].shift(1)) A rolling window that includes the current outcome predicts itself. Filtering away tests with no recent runs can bias a report toward healthy frequently executed tests. Imputing absent modules with zero failure rate gives invented evidence. Inspect the feature’s timestamp against the target timestamp. Check join multiplication, unmatched keys, and whether retries have been mistaken for separate test identities. Compare segment-level duration distributions before labeling an overall slowdown.  Build a CI health report with per-module counts, first-attempt pass rates, mixed-outcome candidates, UTC daily trends, and rejected records. Supply a small hand-calculated fixture to verify the pivot and lag behavior. Feature engineering for the failure classifier should use only what was known when the run failed. Report the forecast horizon and validation split so another engineer can reproduce the apparent gain.

title: CI-health report: reruns, denominators and slow tests
text:
A useful CI-health report combines pass rate, failure frequency, slow-test summaries and data-quality warnings under one declared unit of analysis. A run-level pass rate counts every execution; a latest-result pass rate counts one result per test/build. Reruns make these different quantities, so name the policy in the report. A flaky candidate needs mixed outcomes under comparable conditions, while a slow-test trend needs time order and context. Avoid turning a historical association into a confirmed product cause. title: Query test runs with explicit semantics
text:
SELECT chooses expressions; FROM supplies relations; WHERE filters rows; GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups; ORDER BY orders the final result. Without ORDER BY, row order is not guaranteed. COUNT(*) counts rows. COUNT(duration) counts non-NULL durations. AVG(duration) ignores NULL. SQL comparisons with NULL produce unknown; use IS NULL, not = NULL. SELECT test_id, COUNT(*) AS runs,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failures
FROM test_runs
GROUP BY test_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY test_id; The lab seeds fictional builds, test_cases, test_runs, failures, and defects in DuckDB-WASM. No server receives your SQL. You can inspect data with SELECT * FROM test_runs. Use GROUP BY for counts by module, CASE for indicators, and HAVING for minimum sample size. A CTE gives an intermediate result a meaningful name. title: Join failures to builds and defects
text:

FROM test_cases tc
LEFT JOIN test_runs tr ON tc.test_id = tr.test_id
GROUP BY tc.test_id, tc.name
ORDER BY tc.name; Join failures to defects using an explicit defect_id when available. A shared time window or module is weaker evidence; describe it as correlation. title: Latest results, ranks, and failure streaks
text:

    PARTITION BY test_id ORDER BY build_id DESC, run_id DESC
  ) AS rn
  FROM test_runs
)
SELECT test_id, status FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY test_id; LAG(status) reads the previous row within the ordered partition; LEAD reads the next. title: Subqueries, CASE, UNION, and query plans
text:

title: Consecutive failures: preserve passes in the window

Filtering to failed rows before a window calculation removes the events that interrupt a streak. Define how reruns within a build are handled before counting consecutive builds. A latest-run policy can select one outcome per test/build; the streak then operates over those selected outcomes.  First rank reruns by run_id descending within test/build and select row one. On the remaining complete history, calculate LAG(status,1) and LAG(status,2) partitioned by test_id and ordered by build_id. Select rows where all three statuses are failed. For strict adjacent build IDs, also compare the lagged build IDs to current minus one and two.  SELECT test_id,status,build_id,
 LAG(status,1) OVER(PARTITION BY test_id ORDER BY build_id) AS prev,

 FROM test_runs
) SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM history h JOIN test_cases c USING(test_id)

title: Distributions, percentiles, and misleading averages
text:
The population is the full set you care about; a sample is the subset you observe. The mean adds values and divides by count. The median is the midpoint after sorting. A few long timeouts can raise the mean far above most requests. Variance summarizes squared deviations from the mean; standard deviation returns to the original unit. Sample variance commonly uses n-1 to estimate population variance. Percentiles summarize tails, but estimates depend on sample size and interpolation policy. import statistics
latency = [100, 110, 120, 125, 900]
print(statistics.mean(latency))  # 271
print(statistics.median(latency))  # 120 Latency is often right-skewed: many fast responses and a few slow ones. A normal-distribution assumption may be a poor fit. Plot or inspect the observed distribution before choosing a method. A p95 from 20 requests is fragile. Report sample count, workload, measurement window, and error rate. Excluding timeouts improves reported latency while hiding the worst outcomes; report them separately and state the censoring policy.  Mean and median describe center, while variance and standard deviation describe spread. Percentiles describe thresholds in an ordered sample under a stated convention. A latency report should include sample count, failure count and tail statistics because dropping timed-out requests can make an outage appear faster. Population variance divides by N when describing the full declared population; sample variance often uses N−1 when estimating population variance under appropriate assumptions. Neither formula fixes a biased sample. Compare cold and warm requests, input lengths and concurrency before attributing a latency shift to a model change. Use a small hand-computed sample to test calculations and retain raw durations for investigating tail events.

title: Conditional probability and base rates
text: P(A|B) is the probability of A among cases where B occurred. It differs from P(B|A). Recall asks how many actual defects were flagged; precision asks how many flags were actual defects. Suppose 1% of 10,000 failures are product defects. A detector catches 90 of 100 defects and falsely flags 5% of the 9,900 others, or 495 cases. Precision is 90/(90+495), about 15.4%, despite 90% recall.  A single binary outcome can be modeled as Bernoulli with probability p. The binomial counts successes in n independent trials with the same p. These assumptions matter: repeated chatbot turns from the same conversation can be correlated. Repeated flaky-test runs under shared infrastructure may fail together during an outage. Treating them as independent evidence produces overly narrow confidence intervals. Resample or analyze at the independent unit, such as build or conversation.  Suppose only 1% of runs are true product defects, a detector finds 90% of them, and it alerts on 5% of non-defects. Among 10,000 runs, about 90 alerts are true positives and 495 are false positives, so positive predictive value is only 90/585, about 15.4%. High sensitivity does not imply trustworthy alerts when the base rate is low. Conditional probabilities depend on what is being conditioned on: P(alert|defect) differs from P(defect|alert). Bernoulli models describe one binary outcome and binomial models count independent trials with a common success probability. Related CI retries violate independence, so choose the sampling unit carefully. Test the Bayes calculation with explicit counts and consider human-review capacity when setting alert thresholds.

title: Is 85% really better than 82%?
text: Model A scores 82% and B scores 85%. The observed difference is three percentage points. Without sample size, dataset composition, pairing, repeated runs, and uncertainty, you cannot judge whether the difference generalizes. Evaluate both versions on the same held-out cases to reduce noise from case difficulty. Analyze per-case differences. A paired bootstrap resamples case IDs and recomputes the mean difference; keep conversational clusters together.  A confidence interval expresses uncertainty under a sampling procedure; it is not a probability that this specific fixed parameter lies in the realized interval. A p-value measures how incompatible the observations are with a specified null model, not the chance that the null is true. Predefine a minimum worthwhile effect and release constraints for latency, cost, safety, and critical slices. A statistically detectable one-point improvement may be worthless if it doubles cost. A non-significant result is not proof of equivalence.  A false positive (Type I error) rejects a true null. A false negative (Type II error) misses a real effect. Repeatedly checking many prompt variants until one passes increases false-positive risk. State the hypothesis and stopping rule first. Keep a final untouched evaluation set, report all important slices, and investigate disagreements with human review. Never cherry-pick the most favorable judge configuration.

title: Bootstrap evaluation differences
text:
A bootstrap treats your observed independent cases as an empirical population. Sample n case indices with replacement, calculate a statistic, repeat many times, and summarize the resulting distribution. For paired evaluation, compute B-A for each case before resampling. Do not sample A and B independently when their scores correspond to the same cases. A percentile interval is useful for exploration but can be inaccurate in small or biased samples. import numpy as np
diff = np.array([0, 1, -1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0], dtype=float)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
means = [rng.choice(diff, size=len(diff), replace=True).mean()
         for _ in range(2000)]
print(np.percentile(means, [2.5, 97.5])) Bootstrap does not repair a biased dataset, a miscalibrated judge, or leakage from tuning on evaluation cases. A narrow interval around a biased score is still misleading. For latency, evaluate comparable workloads and resample independent sessions when requests share a session. For correctness, retain human-adjudicated failures and report uncertainty for critical slices separately.  Bootstrap intervals depend on the data representing the target population and on the resampling unit. Resampling individual retries from the same incident treats correlated observations as independent and can make intervals too narrow. A grouped bootstrap samples incidents, retaining their associated observations together. A fixed seed permits a reproducible teaching result but does not establish interval coverage for every distribution or tiny sample. Compare paired candidate-minus-baseline scores within each case before resampling paired differences. Report effect size and interval, not only whether zero is excluded. Test one observation, constant observations and a skewed sample; explain which conclusions remain uncertain when the dataset is small or unrepresentative.

title: Confidence intervals, power, and A/B experiments
text:
A sample estimates a population; uncertainty depends on the sampling process and the independent unit. A 95% confidence procedure covers the fixed parameter in 95% of repeated samples under its assumptions. It does not assign 95% probability to this realized interval. A hypothesis test compares evidence with a specified null model. Type I error rejects a true null; Type II error misses a real effect. Statistical power depends on effect size, noise, sample size, and the decision threshold.  Pre-register the minimum practical improvement, dataset slices, randomization unit, stopping rule, and safety constraints. Use a paired test when both models answer the same cases; randomize users or sessions for an online A/B test when turns share context. For a proportion, a Wilson interval is often more stable near zero or one than the normal approximation. For paired differences, resample independent case or conversation IDs. State the method and assumptions with the score. import math
def wilson(successes,n,z=1.96):
    if n <= 0: raise ValueError("positive sample size required")
    p=successes/n
    center=(p+z*z/(2*n))/(1+z*z/n)
    half=z*math.sqrt(p*(1-p)/n+z*z/(4*n*n))/(1+z*z/n)
    return center-half,center+half
print(wilson(85,100)) Repeatedly testing many prompt variants until one appears significant raises false-positive risk. Check treatment assignment, missing outcomes, judge consistency, and sample ratio mismatch. Do not interpret an inconclusive result as proof of equivalence; define an equivalence margin and gather enough evidence for that question. Report effect size in percentage points and say whether it crosses the predefined useful threshold. title: Formulate a failure-classification problem
text:
Machine learning estimates a mapping from observed features to a target using examples. Supervised learning has labels; unsupervised learning discovers structure without a predefined target. A classifier chooses a category, a regressor predicts a numeric value, and anomaly detection flags unusual observations without proving a defect. For CI failures, define PRODUCT_DEFECT, AUTOMATION_DEFECT, ENVIRONMENT, TEST_DATA, and UNKNOWN. Label by evidence available to expert triage, record disagreements, and retain UNKNOWN instead of forcing false certainty. Define the prediction moment before choosing features.  Build one record per independent incident with log text, runtime context, label, timestamp, and group ID. Separate same-incident retries into the same split. Establish a majority-class or deterministic keyword baseline before a learned model. Feature extraction turns text and metadata into numbers: TF-IDF for log tokens, numeric duration, and one-hot environment categories. Fit preprocessing only on training examples in a Pipeline. Validate on later incidents or held-out groups to approximate real deployment. from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
model=Pipeline([("tfidf",TfidfVectorizer()),("classifier",LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced",max_iter=1000))])
# model.fit(train_logs, train_labels); evaluate only on held-out incidents A resolved defect ID or eventual owner is not available at failure time and leaks the answer. A useful classifier needs a review path for uncertain cases and a failure taxonomy that reflects meaningful routing decisions. title: Preprocessing, cross-validation, and generalization
text:
Training fits parameters, validation selects architecture and thresholds, and a final test set estimates the behavior of the selected system. Overfitting captures accidental training patterns; underfitting misses useful structure. Bias is systematic error from restrictions, while variance reflects sensitivity to the sample. Cross-validation trains and validates repeatedly on different folds. It does not excuse leakage: time order, incident grouping, and transformation fitting still matter. A scaler or vocabulary fitted on all records exposes validation information.  Use GroupKFold for related incident records or a time-based split for changing releases. Put imputation, encoding, feature selection, and estimator in a Pipeline so each fold fits them only on its training partition. Compare learning curves: a persistent poor fit on both train and validation suggests insufficient representation or excessive regularization; a strong train score and weak validation score suggests overfit, shift, or leakage. Keep the final test set untouched until model selection is complete. from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=3)
# for train_idx,val_idx in cv.split(X,y,groups=incident_ids):
#     fold_model.fit(X[train_idx],y[train_idx])
#     score=fold_model.score(X[val_idx],y[val_idx]) Scaling before the split and selecting features using test labels both invalidate the result. A benchmark can also fail without leakage when a new service produces vocabulary absent from training. Break performance down by time, module, and environment. Compare model confidence with actual correctness, inspect mislabeled samples, and measure an abstention policy rather than hiding unknown categories.  Repeat model selection on reproducible folds and report mean and variation with the grouping strategy. Serialize the entire transformation pipeline and its vocabulary, not only model coefficients. This is the ML version of test-environment parity: the code used to transform production input must match the code that generated the reported evaluation result.

title: Linear models, neighbors, trees, and ensembles
text:
Linear regression fits a numeric target by combining weighted features. Logistic regression applies a sigmoid or multiclass softmax to linear scores to model class probabilities; its name does not mean it predicts a continuous regression target. k-NN votes among nearby observations and depends strongly on representation and scaling. A decision tree repeatedly partitions features into regions and can express interactions, but a deep tree overfits. Random forests average many randomized trees to reduce variance. Gradient boosting adds learners that correct remaining errors, often requiring careful regularization and validation.  Choose a model based on feature type, dataset size, interpretability, and operational budget. Start with a regularized linear text model; compare tree ensembles on meaningful numeric/categorical features. Use standardized distances for k-NN and evaluate memory and query time because it retains training examples. Tune depth, regularization, and ensemble size using validation rather than the final test set. For regression report MAE in original units, RMSE to emphasize large mistakes, and R² relative to a mean predictor; R² can be negative. from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error,mean_squared_error,r2_score
y=[2.,4.,6.]
p=[2.,3.,7.]
print(mean_absolute_error(y,p))
print(mean_squared_error(y,p)**.5)
print(r2_score(y,p)) A tree can memorize a build ID that merely correlates with one incident. k-NN can call logs similar because of frequent boilerplate. An ensemble can improve average score while worsening the rare category engineers care about. Inspect feature importance cautiously: importance does not establish causality, and correlated features divide or distort attribution. Run ablations and compare errors before choosing complexity.  Use one preprocessing and evaluation protocol across candidate models. Compare per-class tradeoffs, stability over releases, inference latency, artifact size, and analyst review time. A simple, calibrated baseline with a reliable UNKNOWN path is often preferable to a more accurate opaque model that routes serious defects confidently to the wrong owner.

title: Confusion matrices, imbalance, and thresholds
text:
Accuracy can be high when a rare class is always missed. A confusion matrix counts actual and predicted categories. For a positive class, precision is TP/(TP+FP), recall is TP/(TP+FN), specificity is TN/(TN+FP), and F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. title: Clustering and anomaly detection for CI triage
text:
Clustering groups observations using a representation and distance rule; it does not assign trustworthy business labels. k-means approximates points with centroids and expects a chosen number of clusters. Density methods can identify noise, while anomaly models flag unusual patterns. An unfamiliar error may be a new product defect, a valid new feature, or merely a changed logging format. Treat novelty as a review signal. The connection to supervised learning is representation: poor features produce misleading clusters and neighbors.  Normalize comparable vectors when cosine-like geometry is appropriate, inspect cluster samples, and join expert labels only for analysis. Compare clusters across time and modules. A distance threshold should be selected using known normal and anomalous cases, not guessed from a chart. Build a baseline anomaly score from duration deviation and use it alongside log novelty. Keep environment and workload changes visible so a deployment does not trigger thousands of false alarms. from statistics import mean,pstdev
durations=[2.,2.1,1.9,2.2]
mu,sd=mean(durations),pstdev(durations)
print((5.-mu)/sd) A cluster can reflect boilerplate or tenant names rather than failure mechanism. Outlier removal before analysis can delete precisely the incidents you wanted to find. title: Neurons, activations, tensors, and initialization
Gradient descent and the learning-rate contract
text:
A derivative measures how a small input change affects a function. A gradient collects derivatives with respect to parameters. Gradient descent updates parameters opposite the gradient to reduce a differentiable loss locally. For L(w)=(w-3)², the derivative is 2(w-3). Learning rate controls step size. Too small can converge slowly; too large can overshoot or diverge. A lower training loss does not alone establish better generalization. The optimization objective and validation objective may differ.  Compute a forward prediction, scalar loss, gradients, and an update. In PyTorch, zero gradients before the next backward call because gradients accumulate by default. Separate the optimizer step from data iteration and log meaningful loss aggregates. An epoch is a pass through training data; a minibatch is a subset used for one update. Shuffling improves stochastic training but keep deterministic seeds and independent evaluation splits for reproducibility. w=0.
for epoch in range(10):
    gradient=2*(w-3)
    w-=.1*gradient
print(w,(w-3)**2) Exploding loss can come from excessive learning rate, unscaled features, invalid labels, or an unstable numerical operation. title: Backpropagation is the chain rule in a graph
text:
Backpropagation efficiently applies the chain rule through a computation graph. It does not search randomly for better weights. For h=w1*x, y=w2*h, and loss=(y-target)², propagate dL/dy=2(y-target), dL/dw2=(dL/dy)*h, and dL/dw1=(dL/dy)*w2*x. Every local operation contributes its derivative. Reusing a parameter means its gradient receives contributions from every path. Automatic differentiation records these operations so a framework can perform the same calculation.  Compute one tiny network by hand, then compare gradients with PyTorch autograd and finite differences. Avoid modifying a tensor needed by backward in place. Detaching a tensor or converting through an external array can sever the computation graph. Gradient checking uses a small epsilon: (L(w+epsilon)-L(w-epsilon))/(2*epsilon). Extremely small epsilon introduces floating-point noise; very large epsilon is a poor local approximation. x,w1,w2,target=2.,.5,3.,1.
h=w1*x
y=w2*h
dy=2*(y-target)
print("dL/dw1",dy*w2*x,"dL/dw2",dy*h) A layer’s parameters may have no gradients because the output was detached, the loss did not depend on them, or gradient tracking was disabled. Use no_grad for evaluation and loss.item for a detached logging scalar. Do not retain the training graph merely to print metrics. title: Train and debug a small PyTorch classifier
text:

Cross-entropy is appropriate for class logits; regression losses serve numeric targets. Dropout randomly suppresses activations during training, weight decay penalizes parameter magnitude, and normalization stabilizes representations. These techniques do not repair leakage or labels that contradict one another.  Build a model with nn.Sequential, use integer class indices, and optimize CrossEntropyLoss with Adam. Call model.train for training and model.eval plus no_grad for validation. Track class support and early-stop based on a held-out criterion. from torch import nn
model=nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8,16),nn.ReLU(),nn.Dropout(.1),nn.Linear(16,5))
loss_fn=nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer=torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(),lr=.001)

Inspect errors per class, not just overall accuracy. Ensure class weights refer to the same category order as the label encoder. title: From CNNs and recurrent networks to attention
text:
A CNN applies shared filters across local neighborhoods, learning patterns independent of their exact position. Pooling trades spatial detail for invariance. For logs, a one-dimensional convolution can detect local token patterns; image applications use spatial dimensions. An RNN updates a hidden state sequentially, sharing parameters across positions. Long chains can struggle with gradients and long-range information. LSTM gates control what enters, persists, and leaves a memory state, reducing some of those difficulties.  Choose architecture by structure: MLP for tabular features, CNN for local patterns, RNN/LSTM for sequences when sequential state is useful. Mask padding and distinguish batch, sequence, and feature axes. Attention can directly combine information from distant positions rather than forcing every dependency through one recurrent state. Transformers make this combination highly parallelizable during training, though autoregressive generation still produces dependent next tokens. def moving_pattern(sequence):
    return [sequence[i]+sequence[i+1] for i in range(len(sequence)-1)]
print(moving_pattern([1,0,1,1])) A model may learn padding artifacts or sequence length instead of failure content. Recurrent hidden state accidentally reused across independent incidents leaks context. Flattening all tokens into an MLP loses positional relationships unless explicitly represented. Test invariants by changing padding, permuting irrelevant boilerplate, and separating incidents. Measure meaningful improvements against simpler representations before choosing an architecture for novelty alone. For AI quality engineering, the main objective is diagnosing representation and state failures, not memorizing architecture names. title: Tokenization: text becomes an indexed sequence
Attention: query, key and value with a causal mask
text:
Attention asks which other positions should contribute to the current position. A query represents what a position seeks; keys describe what each position offers; values contain the information to aggregate. Compute query-key dot products, scale by the square root of key dimension, apply the permitted-position mask, then softmax each query row. The output is a weighted sum of values, not the selected key or a database lookup. In a failure log, the word timeout may attend to database rather than unrelated login text. Learned projections determine this behavior; a diagram illustrates a mechanism, not a proof that a model understands a cause.  For one query q=[1,0], keys [[1,0],[0,1]] and values [[4,0],[0,2]], unscaled scores are [1,0]. Softmax gives approximately [0.731,0.269], so the output is [2.924,0.538]. Scaling changes the weights. Subtract the maximum score before exponentiating for numerical stability. Decoder self-attention masks future positions with negative infinity before softmax. Padding masks prevent empty slots from absorbing weight. Each head has its own projections; concatenated heads pass through an output projection, allowing different relationships without assuming each head has a fixed human label. import math
def softmax(scores):
    m=max(scores)
    e=[math.exp(s-m) for s in scores]
    return [v/sum(e) for v in e]
print(softmax([1,0])) A mask applied after softmax without renormalizing leaves a row sum below one. A transposed key matrix or wrong softmax axis mixes batch examples instead of positions. Test shape contracts, finite weights, nonnegative weights and row sums of one. A decoder trained with visible future tokens can show excellent training loss and fail during generation. Check that perturbing a future token cannot change earlier outputs in evaluation mode.  Use the attention calculator to vary scores and observe normalized weights and the value mixture. Implement stable softmax and test extreme scores such as [1000,1001]. The stability test is an SDET boundary check with a mathematical invariant. title: Transformer blocks: position, residuals and encoder–decoder roles
text:
Attention alone is permutation equivariant: swapping input positions swaps outputs without expressing order. Positional information supplies order through learned embeddings, sinusoidal encodings or rotary mechanisms. A transformer block combines attention with a position-wise feed-forward network, residual connections and normalization. Residual paths let gradients flow without replacing the entire representation at every layer. An encoder can see both directions and produce representations for classification or retrieval. A causal decoder predicts the next token from preceding tokens. An encoder-decoder model reads a source sequence and generates a target with cross-attention to encoded source positions.  Track shapes before code: token IDs [batch,length], hidden vectors [batch,length,width], per-head Q/K/V [batch,heads,length,head_width]. Project width into head dimensions, form scores [batch,heads,length,length], then return to hidden width. Feed-forward layers expand and contract each position's width. The runnable lab uses torch.nn.TransformerEncoderLayer and an explicit padding mask. Inspect train/eval behavior because dropout changes repeated outputs. Persist vocabulary, positional convention and maximum length with the checkpoint. import torch
from torch import nn
layer=nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=16,nhead=4,batch_first=True)
layer.eval()
x=torch.zeros(2,5,16)
with torch.no_grad():
    assert layer(x).shape == (2,5,16) Confusing an embedding encoder with a generation decoder produces an integration mismatch: sentence vectors are not next-token distributions. Forgetting positional information can make two differently ordered log messages nearly indistinguishable. A successful tensor shape does not prove a correct mask. Test padding invariance and causal invariance, then compare held-out quality. Length-dependent failures often indicate truncation or positional limits rather than random provider errors.  Sketch the failure-classification encoder path and the support-answer decoder path with input/output shapes. Explain why cross-attention is appropriate for source-to-target generation and why sentence embeddings need a pooling strategy. For an SDET, architecture knowledge enables focused tests: permutation sensitivity, padding invariance, finite outputs, and reproducible evaluation mode. These contracts complement task-level precision and evidence correctness.

title: Next-token training: shifted targets and cross-entropy
text:
A causal language model learns to predict the next token from the preceding sequence. Training pairs logits at position t with the observed token at t+1. Cross-entropy penalizes assigning low probability to the observed target. This objective teaches statistical continuation, not factual verification or authorization. Pretraining supplies broad text patterns; instruction tuning changes task-following examples; preference/reward methods influence which responses are favored. These stages differ in data and objective, and none removes the need for evidence-grounded application checks.  For a target token assigned probability .25, the negative log-likelihood is −log(.25), about 1.386 nats. Average over valid target positions, excluding padded or intentionally masked labels. In a causal model, the library may perform the shift internally; inspect the model contract before shifting twice. The local PyTorch mechanisms lab demonstrates logits, loss and gradients, while the genuine PEFT example adapts a pretrained encoder for the five-class task. Keep classification fine-tuning distinct from causal language-model supervised tuning. import math
probability_of_target=.25
loss=-math.log(probability_of_target)
assert abs(loss-1.38629436112)<1e-9 A developer aligns each position with itself, allowing input-token copying rather than next-token prediction. Another applies softmax before a cross-entropy function expecting logits. Padding contributes loss and dominates short examples. Test shifted alignment, masked positions, finite loss and gradient flow. Use a hand-computed two-token probability example as an independent loss oracle.  A decreasing loss proves optimization progress under the training objective, not better grounded answers. Evaluate the downstream task and safety contract on independent examples after any adaptation. SDETs should retain objective, target alignment and masking configuration in training artifacts. title: Position information and causal invariance tests
text:
A sequence model must distinguish database failed after login from login failed after database. Token embeddings identify symbols, while positional mechanisms encode their order. Sinusoidal encodings use different frequencies by dimension; learned positional embeddings use a trained table; rotary embeddings transform queries and keys to express relative position relationships. These mechanisms have different extrapolation behavior and configuration. A larger advertised context window is not achieved by simply appending zeros to the positional table.  For a simple sinusoidal demonstration, encode even coordinates with sin(pos/10000^(2i/d)) and odd coordinates with cos of the same angle. Add the position vector to the token representation in the classic formulation. Rotary mechanisms instead rotate paired coordinates in attention projections. To test a causal decoder, compare early-position outputs before and after changing a later token in eval mode. Their equality within numerical tolerance verifies the mask's information-flow contract. Padding tests similarly perturb only masked positions. import math
def position(pos):
    return [math.sin(pos),math.cos(pos),math.sin(pos/100),math.cos(pos/100)]
assert position(0)==[0.,1.,0.,1.] A decoder's triangular mask is inverted, exposing future tokens. The test uses dropout in training mode and incorrectly attributes random differences to the mask. An index off-by-one assigns the same position to two adjacent tokens. Control random state and evaluation mode, inspect the permitted-position matrix and test sequences of several lengths including one. Shape tests alone do not detect future-information leakage.  Keep positional configuration and tokenizer revision with model artifacts. Report how truncation and longer sequences affect task quality rather than assuming every allowed position is equally useful. An SDET can test position mechanisms with invariants: different positions have different encodings in the valid range, output dimensions are stable and future perturbations cannot influence earlier causal outputs. These checks isolate architecture behavior from semantic answer evaluation.

title: Pretraining, instruction tuning and grounded generation
text:
Pretraining learns a next-token distribution from many sequences. Instruction tuning trains responses to instructions, while preference or reward-based alignment changes which responses are favored. These stages can improve behavior without making the model an authoritative database. A foundation model can be adapted to many tasks; a task classifier produces a narrower output contract. At inference, the decoder repeatedly predicts a distribution for the next token and appends a selected token. A fluent explanation of a CI failure can still invent an owner because the training objective rewards plausible sequences rather than verified access to your repository. Supply current failure records with stable evidence IDs, require an UNKNOWN classification when insufficient evidence exists, and validate typed output. Keep an independent deterministic source lookup for citations. The local provider adapter records model, prompt version, token counts and finish reason. Live mode uses environment credentials; offline fixtures are explicitly labeled and never described as a live LLM result. result={'category':'UNKNOWN','evidence_ids':[],'needs_review':True}
assert result['category']!='UNKNOWN' or result['needs_review'] A team interprets low temperature as factual accuracy. title: Temperature, top-p and repeatability
text:
Temperature rescales logits before softmax. Lower positive temperature concentrates probability on high-logit tokens; higher temperature spreads it. Top-p keeps the smallest ranked prefix whose cumulative probability reaches p, then renormalizes before sampling. These operations change selection behavior, not the truth of a claim. Greedy decoding chooses an argmax, yet provider behavior can still vary with model revisions, tie breaking and execution. Reproducibility means controlling and recording the relevant configuration, then measuring the remaining variation.  Take probabilities [0.6,0.3,0.1]. At p=0.8 the nucleus includes the first two tokens because 0.6 is insufficient and 0.9 reaches the threshold. Their renormalized probabilities are two-thirds and one-third. Sort by descending probability before accumulating. For classification, prefer a typed enum with explicit abstention and measure class stability across repeated calls. For test generation, allow variation but measure requirement coverage and executable correctness. Keep generation parameters in the experiment manifest. def nucleus(probs,p):
    ranked=sorted(enumerate(probs),key=lambda x:-x[1])
    selected=[];mass=0
    for i,v in ranked:
        selected.append(i);mass+=v
        if mass>=p:break
    return selected Selecting every token below probability p confuses a per-token threshold with cumulative mass. Applying temperature to already normalized probabilities without the correct transformation changes the distribution incorrectly. Repeat the same input enough times to estimate variability and record request configuration. Never mark a test flaky merely because wording changes if the semantic contract remains satisfied.  The decoding calculator exposes temperature and nucleus membership. Implement the nucleus rule with deterministic ordering, check p in (0,1], and test p=1 as a boundary. Record the preserved probability mass before normalization. An AI regression gate should test supported claims, forbidden actions and schema rather than exact prose. Exact comparisons remain appropriate for deterministic application outputs such as canonical enums and sorted IDs.

title: Model selection: quality, context, latency and cost
text:
Choose models against a workload contract rather than a popularity ranking. A failure classifier needs enum accuracy, calibration and low latency; a complex investigation needs multi-step evidence use and safe tools. Context capacity is an input/output budget, not a promise that every token is equally usable. Distracting evidence can reduce quality before the nominal limit is reached. Reasoning-oriented models may spend additional computation or tokens internally. Compare observed end-to-end latency and billed usage using the provider's returned accounting, rather than assuming all models have identical controls or output behavior.  Create a paired benchmark over fixed cases with model ID, provider, prompt hash, tokenizer revision, retrieval version and generation parameters. Measure accepted accuracy, abstention, p95 latency, rate-limit frequency and cost per accepted task. Account for failed requests and retries. Cost=(input_tokens*input_rate + output_tokens*output_rate)/1_000_000 when rates are quoted per million. Treat cached-token discounts and reasoning usage according to returned provider fields. Store rates as dated configuration rather than hardcoded current facts. def cost(input_tokens,output_tokens,input_rate,output_rate):
    return (input_tokens*input_rate+output_tokens*output_rate)/1_000_000
assert cost(1000,500,2,8)==.006 A cheaper model doubles retries and review labor, raising cost per useful answer. A bigger context includes unauthorized documents, increasing both security risk and price. A cache keyed only by user question returns one tenant's answer to another. Test cache scope using tenant, principal permissions, prompt/model versions and index generation. Distinguish cold and warm latency, and retest after a provider revision even when the public alias stays unchanged.  Compare candidates on a held-out set and choose a Pareto frontier: no candidate simultaneously improves quality, cost and latency over another. State constraints first, then reject candidates that violate safety or latency limits. Use the cost calculator to estimate per-call and monthly spend, then replace estimates with measured usage from the local benchmark. A release decision includes uncertainty and a rollback model, not only an average score.

title: Non-determinism: contract stability versus wording changes
text:
Repeated LLM calls can differ because of sampling, provider/model revisions and execution details. A test should distinguish harmless surface variation from changes in the task contract. Two paraphrased supported answers can both pass; two different classification enums cannot both satisfy the same fixed label expectation. Low temperature often reduces sampling variation but does not prove exact repeatability or factual accuracy. Stable hallucinations are still wrong.  Repeat a fixed case with recorded provider/model, prompt, retrieval and generation settings. Normalize only fields whose equivalence is justified, such as whitespace in presentation text; retain canonical category, citations and tool actions unchanged. Measure accepted-decision agreement and per-run correctness. For semantic answers, apply a calibrated rubric to each response and inspect disagreements. Report repetitions and variability alongside the average rather than selecting the best-looking sample. outputs=['ENVIRONMENT','ENVIRONMENT','UNKNOWN']
agreement=max(outputs.count(x) for x in set(outputs))/len(outputs)
assert agreement==2/3 A suite compares exact prose and marks safe paraphrases flaky. Another normalizes away changed evidence IDs, making unsupported answers look equivalent. A team reruns a failing case until it passes and reports only the success. Retain every attempt and define a pass policy before running. Test normalization with meaningful counterexamples and separate provider instability from deterministic application defects.  Acceptance describes the semantic contract, sampling policy and observed variation. For high-risk decisions, explicit review or abstention may be appropriate when repeated accepted outputs disagree. SDETs bring familiar flake discipline: reproduce the variation, identify its layer and avoid masking a real regression with retries. AI variability changes the oracle, not the need for transparent evidence.

title: Context degradation, stale knowledge and explicit abstention
text:
A model's training knowledge can be stale, and long context can contain distractions or contradictions. The context limit is an operational budget, not a promise of perfect use of every included fact. A support answer should use current authorized evidence and state uncertainty when no reliable source supports the claim. Instruction priority defines behavior, while evidence supplies facts. Retrieved text can contain instructions or outdated rules; relevance alone does not establish freshness or trust.  Build cases with a current guide, an obsolete contradictory guide, missing evidence and a malicious instruction embedded in a relevant document. Version sources, filter deleted/unauthorized records and pack current evidence with clear IDs. Require an explicit abstained/review status when support is inadequate. Compare answer support before and after adding irrelevant context, holding model and prompt fixed. Record retained evidence IDs and token usage to distinguish retrieval failure from context degradation. current=[d for d in documents if not d['deleted'] and d['version']==required_version]
status='abstained' if not current else 'candidate' A larger context budget includes an obsolete rule and changes a correct answer. A session summary turns uncertainty into certainty. A cache returns an answer from a previous index generation. Test contradiction, freshness, truncation and revocation. Avoid a repair loop that simply asks for a more confident response; it cannot create missing evidence.  Acceptance reports supported-claim rate and abstention behavior by evidence slice. Current knowledge is maintained through retrieval/source governance, while prompt/model evaluation measures use of that evidence. For SDETs, a no-answer case can be a successful test. The service should fail the user task truthfully rather than produce a fabricated answer that appears to satisfy a shallow text assertion.

title: Provider adapters: deadlines and bounded retries
text:
An adapter isolates provider-specific request and response formats from domain logic. The domain asks for a typed classification; the adapter authenticates, sends the request, normalizes usage and translates errors. Keep credentials on the server, obtained from environment variables or a secret manager. Browser storage and exported progress must never contain a provider key. A timeout limits one attempt; a deadline limits the whole operation, including waiting and retries. Without a deadline, three nominal ten-second attempts plus backoff can violate a fifteen-second service objective.  Classify errors before retrying: transport failures, 429 and selected 5xx responses may be transient; malformed input, authorization failure and unsupported schemas usually require correction. Use capped exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After, and stop before the remaining deadline cannot cover another attempt. Retry only operations whose effects are safe to repeat. For tool side effects, use a persisted idempotency key. Record attempt count, provider request ID, elapsed time and final error without logging credentials or full sensitive prompts. def retryable(status):
    return status == 429 or 500 <= status < 600
assert not retryable(401) Catching every Exception and retrying an invalid API key multiplies latency without any chance of success. Retrying a tool after a network timeout can execute the same write twice even when the client never received the first result. Inject failures at the HTTP boundary with a mock transport. Assert that 401 has one attempt, 429 honors the retry policy, the deadline terminates work, and cancellation is propagated rather than swallowed.  The local provider lab exposes identical typed results from live and deterministic fixture adapters, with mode recorded in every report. Fixture mode tests application behavior; live mode measures model behavior and requires explicit environment credentials. Gate releases on malformed-response handling, authentication isolation and timeout behavior before evaluating classification quality. A valid model answer that arrives after the application deadline is not a successful user task.

title: Streaming and bounded concurrent inference
text:
Streaming emits a sequence of events before the final response exists. First-token latency describes responsiveness, while end-to-end latency includes the full completion. A partial JSON fragment is not a typed domain result. Treat transport events, assembled output and final validated response as separate objects. Concurrency overlaps waiting; it does not remove rate limits. A semaphore bounds in-flight work while a queue bounds pending work. Backpressure prevents a traffic spike from consuming unbounded memory.  Use asynchronous clients, connection pooling, an overall deadline and cancellation on client disconnect. Assemble deltas in order, retain a finish reason, and validate only the final payload. A streaming error must end the UI in a visible failed or partial state. Track queue time separately from provider time. Set limits for per-tenant concurrency, output tokens and queue length. Retries enter the same capacity budget as first attempts so outages do not create a retry storm. events=['{"category":', '"UNKNOWN"}']
assembled=''.join(events)
import json
assert json.loads(assembled)['category']=='UNKNOWN' An API returns success when the first stream event arrives, then ignores a truncated stream. Another implementation opens hundreds of connections with gather over an unbounded list. Both can pass a single happy-path test. Test duplicate events, missing completion events, cancellation, abrupt disconnects and queue saturation. Ensure cancellation releases permits and that a partial response is not cached as a complete answer.  Replay a recorded event sequence through the adapter and measure TTFT, final latency and validation status. Load tests must include long outputs and slow clients, not only short classifications. For SDET evidence, report in-flight maximum, rejected queue entries and whether every completed result passed schema validation. Separate capacity failures from model-quality failures in the release report.

title: Normalize provider outcomes without hiding failures
text:
