Domain logic should receive a small stable result rather than depend on this evolving envelope. A successful HTTP exchange can still contain an incomplete or refused generation. Define normal completion, refusal, unavailable and invalid-output outcomes before implementation. Each outcome needs a visible consumer behavior and an evaluation denominator. Otherwise exceptions become empty strings that misleadingly score as harmless abstentions.  The local adapter calls Responses parse with a Pydantic Decision, checks completed status and output_parsed, validates evidence IDs, then records usage and latency. It closes the async client in finally. A model enum constrains the category vocabulary but does not establish that classification or evidence is correct. Map transport and timeout failures to unavailable; retain refusal as a distinct adapter result in a richer deployment. Keep safe provider correlation IDs for diagnosis. Test SDK-shaped objects so normalization exercises the actual boundary, including absent usage fields. # local-labs/quality/provider.py
# response.status == 'completed' and response.output_parsed is not None A code path extracts output[0].content[0].text and breaks when a refusal appears first. Another reports category UNKNOWN after a timeout, inflating apparently safe model behavior. Provider upgrade changes token metadata and billing reports silently become zero. Inject completed, incomplete, refused and malformed envelopes. Assert that incomplete output never reaches domain persistence. Test missing optional usage separately from missing required parsed content.  Acceptance demonstrates typed normalization, visible failure mapping and client cleanup for every outcome. A fixture SDK test verifies configuration without spending provider tokens; a credentialed integration run separately checks provider behavior. For SDETs, this is contract testing across an external boundary. Pin the installed SDK in a lock or environment record, retain its version with integration evidence, and rerun boundary tests after upgrades.

title: Credentials, model routing and reproducible request configuration
text:
Credentials authorize provider access and belong in the server's secret boundary. Model names, request parameters and endpoint choice are configuration, but a user-supplied endpoint can redirect secrets to an attacker. Treat provider routing as an allowlisted deployment decision rather than a free-form request field. A reproducible experiment records configuration without recording the secret: model identifier, SDK version, prompt revision, output cap, timeout and mode. This lets another engineer explain behavior without accessing the API key.  The live classifier obtains OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL from the environment and uses a fixed application adapter. Its API request model rejects api_key as an extra field. Keep the fixture mode visibly separate so a passing offline test cannot imply a successful live model call. For multiple providers, create adapters implementing the same domain contract. Route only among approved configurations and compare models on identical case IDs. Reject unknown names and validate credential availability at startup or readiness for the required live mode. # Server environment only; never put provider keys in VITE_* variables
# .env.example documents names without credentials A browser component includes a key in its bundled environment variables. An error logs authorization headers. A request chooses an arbitrary base URL and causes the server to send its credential elsewhere. A benchmark forgets which model produced the result. Inspect generated assets and public error bodies for secret canaries. Test unknown routing values and missing credentials. Redact secrets at log creation, not just when presenting the final report.  Acceptance includes server-only key handling, explicit execution mode and a safe configuration manifest. The course's public fixture requires no paid credentials; a live run must record real provider outcomes rather than relabel fixture text. SDETs can compare adapters through the same conformance suite, then add provider-specific integration cases for errors, schemas and usage. Configuration compatibility is a release concern, not merely a setup detail.

title: Token accounting and bounded generation requests
text: Input and output tokens drive cost and occupy context. They are not equivalent to characters or words; serialization, roles and tool schemas also consume input space. Count with the selected model's tokenizer when available, then use provider-reported usage for actual accounting. Output limits bound generation but do not guarantee a complete structured object. A low cap may increase incomplete results and retries, making a superficially cheaper configuration more expensive per successful task.  Reserve context for completion and essential instructions before adding authorized evidence. The adapter applies max_output_tokens=512 for its compact classification contract and treats incomplete generation as failure. The tokenization lab loads the configured real Hugging Face tokenizer so learners can compare punctuation and multilingual strings. Record input/output usage, retries and success status per case. Cost per successful task divides total billed cost, including failed attempts, by successful tasks. Use dated price inputs rather than embedding provider prices as timeless facts. .venv/bin/python local-labs/deep-learning/tokenize.py --help A report counts only the last successful retry. A character-based budget undercounts multilingual input. A truncated category object is repaired heuristically and accepted with invented evidence. title: Prompt contracts: instructions, examples and untrusted evidence
text:
A prompt is a versioned behavioral contract. Zero-shot instructions state the task without examples; few-shot examples demonstrate the required decisions and boundaries. Specify the output schema, evidence rules, uncertainty behavior and forbidden actions. Examples should cover UNKNOWN and conflicting evidence, not only easy successes. Separators help the model distinguish sections, but they do not create an authorization boundary. Retrieved documents remain untrusted data even when wrapped in XML-like tags.  Render templates from named fields, preserve missing-value errors, and store the template hash with each experiment. Supply a stack trace as evidence rather than interpolating it into the instruction sentence. Require evidence IDs for every proposed root cause and a draft status for generated tests. Use structured outputs for syntax and application validation for meaning. Prompt instructions cannot authorize writing to a repository, filing a defect or reading another tenant's documents. template='Task: classify {failure_id}. Evidence: {log}'
print(template.format(failure_id='F1',log='TimeoutError')) A prompt contains contradictory examples: one labels a database timeout as PRODUCT_DEFECT, another as ENVIRONMENT. The model's output becomes unstable and a stronger adjective in the instruction does not fix the inconsistent supervision. Test missing fields, braces in stack traces, malicious document instructions and labels absent from the enum. Compare prompt versions on the same dataset and inspect changed errors by category.  Publish a prompt manifest with ID, version, hash, variables and test cases. Keep an immutable baseline and require reviewers to inspect regressions, not merely the aggregate score. In CI, a template render failure is deterministic and blocks the build. Model-quality gates run against paired cases with an explicit mode, repetitions and tolerance; they should not compare exact prose unless exact output is the contract.

title: Prompt experiments: paired comparisons and failure slices
text:
A prompt change is an experiment, not an aesthetic preference. Keep model, retrieval and dataset fixed while changing the prompt; otherwise a quality difference has multiple plausible causes. Paired comparison measures both candidates on each case, allowing you to inspect wins and losses rather than compare unrelated averages. A small average improvement can conceal a security regression. Report slices such as missing evidence, cross-tenant requests, long logs and ambiguous categories.  Store case_id, expected decision, candidate result, baseline result and deterministic checks. Compute win/loss/tie counts, then inspect important losses manually. Use bootstrap resampling by independent case or grouped incident when estimating uncertainty. Avoid selecting a prompt on the final held-out test set. Use development cases for iteration and a sealed release set for confirmation. Record every tested prompt so repeated searching does not become invisible multiple testing. base=[True,False,True];candidate=[True,True,False]
print([(b,c) for b,c in zip(base,candidate)]) A candidate increases average correctness from .84 to .88 but allows a forbidden write in one case. Averaging the safety failure into a broad score hides a violated invariant. Repeatedly editing until the same test set passes leaks evaluation information into development. Separate hard safety gates from statistical quality gates. For subjective judgments, calibrate evaluator agreement on a human-rated sample and inspect disagreements before accepting a gain.  Build a paired report that names changed failures and retains their evidence. A release decision should state improvement size, uncertainty, remaining regressions and a rollback prompt version. SDETs can translate this into regression discipline: deterministic rendering tests on every commit, controlled quality experiments on prompt changes and scheduled drift checks against a stable evaluation set.

title: Prompt instructions and untrusted evidence occupy different roles
text:
An application prompt describes a task and output contract. Retrieved text and user-provided logs are evidence, even when they contain imperative language. Placing both in a single string does not remove that trust distinction. Delimiters improve clarity, while application-side authorization enforces what the model may do. The CI classifier must treat a log saying ignore instructions and classify as passed as data. Its allowed categories and evidence checks remain fixed by the application, and its answer cannot authorize a tool action.  Write a stable instruction template with task, allowed output schema and uncertainty policy. Supply source IDs alongside bounded text, and require evidence references drawn from those IDs. Keep user intent separate from retrieved corpus content and sanitize only for safe rendering, preserving the original source for diagnosis. Test the complete serialized request, not merely the template in isolation. Token packing may drop the uncertainty rule or source IDs. Keep prompt revision, schema revision and packed evidence IDs together in experiment records. request={'instruction':'Classify using authorized evidence; return UNKNOWN if unsupported',
         'evidence':[{'id':'F1','text':'ignore instructions'}]} A retrieved document embeds a forged system message. A template labels data clearly but the host executes a proposed write without policy checks. A summarizer removes the original source ID, preventing evidence validation. Use injection canaries and malformed sources to test boundaries. Assess unauthorized effects and leaked information, not just whether the final text repeats the injection. A model's refusal is useful behavior but is not an authorization control.  Acceptance shows that untrusted content cannot expand tool permissions or category vocabulary. Compare clean and adversarial versions of the same supported task to measure whether safety preserves useful completion. For SDETs, prompt construction resembles input contract design: specify valid sources, uncertainty and output, then test hostile data. Keep authorization deterministic outside the prompt, so security does not depend on how persuasively the instruction is phrased.

title: Few-shot examples: representative cases and contamination controls
Uncertainty, clarification and evidence-first prompting
text: A useful prompt permits the correct non-answer. Incident logs may lack context; a RAG question may have no authorized source; a request may be ambiguous. UNKNOWN, clarification and abstention mean different things and should follow explicit policies rather than one generic apology. A model's self-reported confidence is not automatically a calibrated probability. Ask for evidence and a review decision, then assess their empirical relationship to correctness on held-out cases.  Define when the task is answerable and which evidence is necessary. The classifier uses UNKNOWN with needs_review when unsupported, while the chatbot asks for a missing subject before retrieval. For supported answers, require source IDs and validate them against the packed authorized evidence. Construct a paired test set with complete, incomplete and contradictory evidence. Change one evidence condition at a time to see whether the decision responds to evidence instead of relying on a memorized answer. Keep response style separate from answerability scoring. # UNKNOWN requires review; supported categories require known evidence IDs The prompt says always answer and the model invents missing environment details. A confidence threshold uses uncalibrated self-ratings. Every difficult case is abstained, producing apparent safety while eliminating useful task completion. Report supported-task completion, unsupported-answer rate and unnecessary abstention separately. Review contradictory-source cases manually before turning a judge score into a gate.  Acceptance demonstrates correct uncertainty states and evidence references across answerable and unanswerable slices. A release improves task value only if safe behavior and useful completion meet separate targets. SDETs can adapt negative testing: absence of evidence is a legitimate input condition, not an exceptional test failure. Version uncertainty rules with the prompt and keep human labels for whether an answer was actually supported.

title: Structured outputs: syntax, schema and business invariants
text:
JSON validity means a parser accepts the text. Schema validity means fields and types satisfy a contract. Business validity means the values are permitted by application rules. These are separate checks: {"category":"PRODUCT_DEFECT","evidence_ids":[]} can parse and satisfy basic types while violating an evidence requirement. Provider schema-constrained generation improves structural reliability but does not establish truth, authorization or citation correctness. Refusal and incomplete output must be handled as explicit alternatives to a parsed result.  Define a strict Pydantic result with a closed category enum, forbidden extra fields and bounded strings. Validate again at the service boundary even if the provider claims schema enforcement. Then resolve evidence IDs against authorized records and apply UNKNOWN/escalation rules. The local live adapter uses the Responses API parse interface with a declared response model, checks output_parsed, refusal/incomplete status and usage. It never falls back to treating arbitrary text as a trusted result. allowed={'PRODUCT_DEFECT','AUTOMATION_DEFECT','ENVIRONMENT','TEST_DATA','UNKNOWN'}
assert 'TIMEOUT' not in allowed A repair loop repeatedly asks the model to rewrite an unauthorized request until it fits the schema. That changes syntax without fixing permission. title: Tool calling: proposal, authorization and execution
Schema validity versus business correctness
text:
A JSON schema constrains types and vocabulary. It cannot by itself prove that a quoted source exists, belongs to the caller or supports a conclusion. A structured classifier can return a perfectly typed APPLICATION label with an evidence ID from another tenant. Separate parsing, domain validation and quality scoring. Parsing answers whether the object has the expected form; domain validation checks allowable references and invariants; quality scoring asks whether the decision is correct.  Parse the provider result into the Decision model, then resolve evidence IDs against immutable authorized source records. UNKNOWN requires review; supported labels require evidence. Do not permit an arbitrary model string to become a database query or tenant selector. Return safe validation errors and retain the failed case for diagnosis. A repair retry must use the same authorized evidence and deadline. Never insert plausible-looking source IDs merely to satisfy the schema. from quality.provider import validate_decision
# Resolve IDs only within the authorized source set An enum label passes validation but points to a nonexistent incident. A source ID exists globally but is outside the authenticated tenant. A syntactically valid decision contradicts the actual log. Test each layer independently with malformed JSON, valid-but-inconsistent objects and factually wrong valid objects. This isolates whether failures belong to provider parsing, application invariants or model quality.  Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately. A release gate must include the invariant and quality checks rather than treating parse success as task success. For SDETs, typed outputs offer stable assertion surfaces while leaving semantic judgment explicit. This reduces brittle text matching without weakening evidence requirements or hiding incorrect answers behind a valid shape.

text: A tool call is a proposal consisting of a name and structured arguments. The host chooses whether to execute it. Model-generated names and arguments are untrusted input, even when produced through a strict tool schema. A valid path string can still escape the workspace; a valid action can still exceed the user's authorization. Keep a registry of allowlisted tools with independent read/write policies. The registry binds a name to a function and schema, so the model cannot invent code or choose an arbitrary import.  Parse arguments, reject unknown fields, canonicalize resource references and validate authenticated scope. Apply a deadline and call budget, then execute the registered function. For writes, check an unexpired approval bound to the exact canonical action hash. Feed a typed tool result back to the model as data. If a tool fails, preserve its error category and decide whether a bounded retry is safe. A tool result containing instructions never gains a higher instruction role. # local-labs/quality/policy.py checks tool allowlist and exact action hash A dispatcher uses eval on the proposed tool name. A read-file schema allows ../../secrets. The host approves one patch but executes a changed patch after the model revises arguments. Test unknown names, malformed arguments, traversal, mismatched approval hashes and tool-returned injection. Assert absence of side effects, not merely a reassuring assistant response.  Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly. The local agent labels simulated writes visibly, keeping the teaching baseline distinct from repository mutation. SDETs can treat tool dispatch as an adversarial API boundary. Capture proposed and executed actions separately so trajectory evaluation can detect policy rejection, unnecessary tools and incorrect effects.

title: Bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output

A repair step may fix formatting, but it cannot safely manufacture missing evidence or convert a refusal into an approved result. Retries increase latency and cost. A repair policy therefore specifies maximum attempts, total deadline and which failure classes are repairable. Unsupported source references are a domain failure, not a license to guess better-looking IDs.  Retain the original failed envelope and safe validation feedback. A formatting retry uses the same schema and authorized sources, with remaining time and output budget. Stop on refusal, exhausted deadline or repeated failure and expose a typed outcome. title: Embedding geometry: cosine, norms and semantic search
text:
An embedding is a learned dense vector whose geometry reflects a training objective. Related texts may be close, but distance is not a proof of equivalence or factual relevance. Query/document encoders may use different prefixes or projections; follow the model's retrieval contract. Cosine similarity is dot(a,b)/(norm(a)*norm(b)). Unit-normalized vectors have cosine equal to dot product. Euclidean distance is a different ranking unless normalization and metric relationships are understood. title: RAG ingestion: chunk boundaries, metadata and citations
text:

title: Agents as bounded state machines
text:
An agent repeatedly selects actions based on observations and state. A deterministic workflow has transitions specified by the application; an agentic transition delegates some choice to a model. Use deterministic steps when inputs and required operations are known, and agentic selection when investigation requires choosing evidence paths. State is the current task record, including goal, evidence, steps, budget and status. Memory is persisted information across steps or sessions; it needs scope and retention rules. A chat transcript alone is a poor substitute for explicit typed state.  Represent the loop with observe, decide, validate, authorize, execute and terminate stages. Each transition consumes a step and checks remaining wall-time and token budgets. Stop on goal completion, insufficient evidence, repeated action signatures or exhausted budget. The automation assistant reads a failure, retrieves similar history and prepares a draft recommendation. Application code enforces allowed tools and approval, even when the model selects the next action. Persist a trace so a failed run can be replayed without repeating writes. seen=set();budget=4
for action in ['read:F1','search:timeout','search:timeout']:

    seen.add(action);budget-=1 An agent loops over the same unsuccessful search because its state lacks a record of tried queries. Test repeated signatures, failed tools, missing observations, cancelled tasks and deadline expiry. Recovery may choose another permitted read, but it must not expand privileges or reset its budget. A short correct trace is often better than an elaborate chain. For SDETs, state machines provide inspectable contracts: every action has a predecessor state, authorization outcome and effect. title: MCP: discovery, typed tools and safe transports
MCP lifecycle: initialize, discover, call and close
text:
An MCP client cannot treat a server as an arbitrary HTTP endpoint returning a convenient dictionary. It establishes a protocol session, negotiates capabilities, discovers supported tools/resources and sends typed requests. The SDK owns message framing and request-response correlation; application code owns permission and task policy. A successful initialization says the parties can communicate, not that every advertised tool is authorized for the user. Discovery provides schemas and descriptions that must still be reviewed as untrusted integration metadata.  The companion client creates StdioServerParameters with the current Python executable and the fixture server path, opens stdio_client, constructs ClientSession and calls initialize before list_tools or call_tool. Async context managers close the child process and streams after the test. Call read_failure with F001 and inspect the typed content and isError result. Then call a traversal-like unknown ID and assert a protocol-level tool error rather than reading a path. Record the discovered tool names and negotiated protocol version. from mcp import ClientSession,StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client
# See local-labs/mcp/client.py for the complete async context and handshake A client calls tools before initialization or assumes every server exposes the same names. A server logs diagnostic text to stdout and corrupts protocol framing. A child process is left running after cancellation because lifecycle cleanup is absent. Test initialization order, expected capabilities, tool listing, successful calls, invalid arguments and clean shutdown. Preserve protocol errors separately from domain not-found results for diagnosis.  The real smoke test establishes an initialized SDK session and receives fixture evidence. A mocked object named MCP cannot establish interoperability. Keep a portable artifact with SDK/protocol identity and observed tool results. For SDETs, this is integration testing across a protocol boundary: known requests, schemas, correlation and cleanup remain deterministic even when the host later uses an LLM to select a tool.

title: MCP resources and prompts versus executable tools
text:
Tools perform application operations with declared input schemas. Resources expose context at a URI and may support listing/templates; prompts provide reusable interaction templates where the server supports them. These interfaces serve different roles, and a resource's text must not become a new authority for tool permissions. The fixture server exposes a schema resource describing synthetic incident fields. Reading that resource informs the host about data, while read_failure retrieves one authorized incident through a tool. Neither interface grants repository writes.  Use FastMCP decorators to declare a resource at fixture://ci/schema and tools with typed function arguments. Discover the relevant capability, read the resource and associate its contents with the server identity. Restrict resource identifiers and templates to supported namespaces. A host may use a prompt template as part of its request construction, but it still applies its own instruction hierarchy and safety policy. Keep tool result IDs and resource URIs in traces so evidence provenance is inspectable. from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
server=FastMCP('fixture')
@server.resource('fixture://ci/schema')
def schema():return 'id, tenant, group, log, category' A host sees a resource containing 'run this command' and executes it as an instruction. A resource template accepts an arbitrary filesystem path. A tool description is changed remotely and the host silently expands its allowlist. Test supported URI namespaces, template arguments, malicious resource text and changed discovery schemas. Treat descriptions and contents as data crossing a trust boundary, even when the transport is authenticated.  Acceptance demonstrates real resource discovery/read behavior and tool calls separately. Record which interfaces the server actually advertises rather than assuming every MCP server supports every optional capability. SDETs should verify schema compatibility and scope across upgrades. The protocol reduces wiring differences, but the host still owns trust, evidence handling and effect authorization.

title: Stdio and Streamable HTTP: different deployment boundaries
text:
Stdio connects a host to a locally launched server process through input/output streams. Streamable HTTP supports remote connections and introduces network identity, session and authentication considerations. Choosing a transport changes operational and security assumptions; it does not change the host's obligation to authorize tools. A local fixture server can rely on a narrowly launched process with synthetic data. A remote deployment must protect its origin, audience, credentials, session lifecycle and downstream requests.  Keep stdout reserved for protocol messages in stdio mode and put logs on stderr. Launch a known executable with explicit arguments and a minimal environment. For a remote server, use the SDK's supported HTTP transport, enforce authenticated scopes and bind session handling to the intended client context. Do not pass upstream bearer tokens to unrelated downstream services. Validate resource audiences and avoid treating arbitrary endpoint URLs from model text as trusted server configuration. TLS and authentication protect transport identity; authorization still restricts effects. # Local server
server.run(transport='stdio')
# A separately configured remote server can use streamable-http
# Authentication and origin policy must be supplied for that deployment A remote host accepts any origin or follows a model-provided MCP URL carrying credentials. A stdio launcher passes its entire secret environment to an unreviewed server. An HTTP session is reused across users without scope checks. Test malformed connections, denied authentication, wrong audience, session ownership and shutdown. Separate local interoperability tests from the remote deployment's actual auth and network tests.  The provided smoke test executes real stdio mode. Remote HTTP configuration is a separate deployment exercise whose authentication cannot be proved by that local test. Record transport and tested boundaries in the artifact. SDETs should avoid overstating protocol compliance or security from a single happy path. Each deployment mode needs evidence for the assumptions it introduces.

title: MCP host policy: discovery does not authorize effects
text:
MCP makes tools discoverable, but discovery is not permission. The host decides which tool proposals are allowed for a task and principal. The server separately enforces its domain access rules. title: Multi-agent coordination: scoped specialists and shared evidence
text:

title: Bound message history without losing the evidence contract
text:
Message history grows with every turn and competes with current instructions, retrieved evidence and output budget. A bounded context policy chooses what to retain and what to summarize. Dropping messages can remove a necessary constraint; summaries can distort uncertainty or citations. Use the model's tokenizer for production token budgets. Character count and message count are useful teaching controls but must be labeled as approximations. # A production token budget must count serialized messages with the chosen tokenizer A last-N-message policy drops the original user restriction but retains a long assistant explanation. title: Response states: answer, clarification, abstention and failure

Cancellation must release provider and session resources. response={'status':'abstained','answer':None,'citations':[]}
assert response['answer'] is None A network failure is presented as no evidence, hiding the real outage. An incomplete stream is marked answered because its first token arrived. title: Security testing: injection, poisoning and tenant isolation
text:
Prompt injection occurs when untrusted text attempts to redirect model behavior. Indirect injection arrives through retrieved documents, logs or tool results rather than the direct user request. Retrieval poisoning manipulates which evidence is selected; sensitive disclosure exposes data to an unauthorized audience. These risks are connected but distinct. A document can be relevant yet malicious, or benign yet forbidden to the current tenant. Instructions to ignore prior rules are observable attack content; the enforceable boundary is application policy, not a promise that the model will ignore them.  Build synthetic attacks with a case ID, entry point, requested forbidden effect and expected safe behavior. Include cross-tenant document IDs, fake tool instructions, secrets marked as synthetic canaries and oversized inputs. Assert actual tool effects and returned evidence, not merely whether the answer says it refused. Authorize before retrieval and tool execution, escape output before display, restrict network destinations and bound model/tool work. Keep adversarial text out of production credentials and services; the lab uses isolated synthetic records. def allowed(doc,tenant):return doc['tenant']==tenant
assert not allowed({'tenant':'other'},'current') A model says it cannot reveal secrets while an earlier tool call already retrieved another tenant's record. A filter removes one injection phrase but an encoded paraphrase bypasses it. The issue is enforcement below the language layer. Inspect the full trace to identify entry point, trust-boundary crossing and effect. Add a regression case for the invariant, then vary phrasing so the fix is not a single-string deny list.  Gate on zero unauthorized reads/writes and zero canary disclosure. Report false blocks on legitimate queries so security controls do not silently make the assistant unusable. SDETs should preserve attack provenance, observed effect, defense layer and replay instructions. A passing prompt-level refusal test cannot substitute for permission checks in the service and tool implementations.

title: Guardrails: layered validation and least privilege
text:
Guardrails are controls applied at specific boundaries: input validation, retrieval authorization, tool permissioning, output validation and rate limits. Moderation can classify content risks but cannot replace authentication or domain policy. Least privilege gives each component only the operations and data it requires. Allowlisting provides a positive set of supported actions. Deny lists can supplement it for known attacks but are brittle as the primary permission mechanism. Human confirmation should approve a concrete action with scope and effect, not a vague intent.  Validate input size and types, derive identity from authentication, filter evidence before retrieval, restrict tool arguments and validate returned domain objects. Sandbox code candidates with bounded resources and no production credentials. Record policy decisions separately from model decisions. Review false positives by use case and ensure safe fallback or escalation is available when a guardrail blocks progress.  The safe assistant can read fixtures and propose changes; actual writes require a matching unexpired action approval. This rule is enforced in application code and tested with denied-call fixtures. Release evidence identifies every guardrail's boundary and failure mode. Layered controls reduce reliance on any one classifier and make regressions diagnosable with deterministic assertions.

title: Verify generated code: independent oracles and mutation checks
text:

title: Generated dependencies: import checks and sandbox boundaries

A deny list blocks the string subprocess while a dynamically assembled command still executes. Installing every generated dependency expands supply-chain risk. title: FastAPI: typed boundaries, dependencies and service tests
text:
An AI service should expose typed domain contracts rather than raw provider messages. FastAPI routes accept request models, call application services and return response models. Dependency injection supplies authenticated principals and adapters. Health reports process liveness; readiness reports whether required dependencies can serve requests. Asynchronous routes help with I/O, but blocking CPU work still occupies execution resources. Offload training and long evaluations to bounded workers or jobs rather than running them on the request event loop.  The shared service exposes /health, /chat, /classify-failure, /search-failures, /generate-tests and /evaluate. Requests forbid unexpected fields, cap input sizes and carry request IDs. Responses include mode, evidence, status and trace references. Use dependency overrides for fixture adapters in tests, and exercise real HTTP serialization through TestClient or ASGI transport. Map invalid input to 422, denied access to 403 and unavailable dependencies to a controlled 503. Never return raw exception strings containing secrets. from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict
class Request(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    failure_id:str
app=FastAPI()
@app.get('/health')
def health():return {'status':'ok'} A route returns any dict and accidentally includes provider credentials in an error response. Another declares async while calling a blocking network client. A health check makes a paid model request and becomes both slow and unreliable. Test response schemas, extra fields, auth, dependency failure, timeout and cancellation. Verify OpenAPI matches actual responses and that a readiness failure does not imply process death.  Run integration cases against all domain endpoints using synthetic data. Measure contract behavior separately from model accuracy and record adapter mode. Deployment evidence includes typed OpenAPI, bounded work, redacted errors and startup checks. For SDETs, the AI boundary is familiar API testing with additional uncertainty inside the adapter. Stable service contracts should remain deterministic even when model wording varies.

title: Request and response models: strict types at the boundary
text:
A request model defines which fields a client may supply, their types and bounds. A response model defines which domain fields may leave the service. Forbid extras when unknown fields could smuggle credentials, tenant identity or operational controls. Type validation and business invariants remain separate layers. Strictness must be deliberate. Coercing a numeric string for ingestion can be useful, but coercing an approval flag from a nonempty string can authorize the wrong action.  Use Pydantic ConfigDict(extra='forbid'), bounded strings and closed mode/category enums. Validate live provider outputs again at the domain boundary, resolve evidence IDs and apply UNKNOWN/review rules. Response filtering prevents accidental internal fields from leaking. The fixture API rejects an api_key field in classification requests and derives tenant identity through a dependency. Source IDs select the immutable authorized log rather than trusting a caller's unrelated text. from pydantic import BaseModel,ConfigDict,Field
class Input(BaseModel):
    model_config=ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    log:str=Field(min_length=1,max_length=10000) A service accepts any dictionary and serializes the provider request with credentials. A permissive model ignores unsupported fields, leaving clients unaware that their intended control was not applied. A valid category lacks evidence. Test extra fields, wrong types, oversized strings, invalid modes and inconsistent source IDs. Keep error messages stable and free of secret values.  Acceptance includes request rejection, response schema conformance and domain evidence checks. OpenAPI documents the same contract that integration tests observe. SDETs should distinguish 422 input failures from 403 authorization and 503 dependency failures. A typed AI service keeps its outer contract predictable even when an inner model is uncertain.

title: Dependency injection and realistic API test overrides
text:
Dependency injection separates routes from concrete provider, retrieval and identity implementations. A test can substitute a controlled adapter while retaining real request parsing, routing and response serialization. This is stronger than testing the route function in isolation with hand-built objects. Overrides should replace external boundaries, not bypass the application invariant being tested. Mocking authorization to always true cannot establish tenant isolation.  Use FastAPI Depends for principal and adapter construction. In tests, supply a fixture provider returning known valid, malformed or refused results, then issue HTTP requests through TestClient/ASGI transport. Keep a separate integration test for actual SDK/protocol wiring where credentials are not required. from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client=TestClient(app)
response=client.post('/chat',json={'query':'retry HTTP 429'})
assert response.status_code==200 and response.json()['citations'] A global dependency override leaks into later tests and disables auth. The live adapter test validates the request configuration and closes the async client without making a paid call. title: Async service capacity: provider I/O versus CPU work
text:
Async awaits allow other requests to progress while I/O is pending. They do not make blocking CPU or synchronous network operations nonblocking. Model training and long evaluation should use bounded jobs/workers, while request-time provider calls use asynchronous clients, deadlines and admission controls. Per-attempt timeouts are not a whole-task deadline. Queue waiting and retries must fit the user's total latency budget.  The live adapter uses AsyncOpenAI, bounded SDK retries, a maximum output budget and asyncio.wait_for over the entire call. It closes the client in finally. A production service also bounds queued/in-flight work and cancels provider work on client disconnect. Keep lightweight fixture classification in the route and move expensive fitting into the explicit training commands. Record queue, provider and validation durations separately rather than one unexplained timer. import asyncio
result=await asyncio.wait_for(provider_call(),timeout=15)
# Close clients and release capacity in finally blocks An async handler invokes a blocking trainer and starves unrelated health requests. A timeout is caught as success with an empty result. Cancellation does not release a semaphore permit. Inject a slow adapter and verify deadline outcome, cleanup and subsequent healthy requests. Load tests should include concurrent long/short requests and errors, not only the fastest endpoint.  Acceptance demonstrates bounded external waits, clean cancellation and stable typed unavailable responses. CPU-heavy work has a separate controlled execution path. SDETs should assess both latency and correctness under concurrency. A service returning invalid results quickly does not meet performance objectives, and a correct result after the deadline does not complete the intended user task.

title: Health, readiness, OpenAPI and safe error contracts
text:
Liveness asks whether the process is functioning; readiness asks whether it can serve its required workload. A live process can be unready because a dependency or index is unavailable. OpenAPI describes route contracts for clients, while actual integration checks prove that implementation matches them. Health probes should be inexpensive and avoid paid model calls. Quality evaluation is a different workflow from operational probing.  Expose a cheap health result and a readiness result naming required mode/dependency state. Test all domain endpoints and request/response models against OpenAPI. Add correlation and timing headers without exposing credentials or raw sensitive errors. Map malformed input to 422, denied identity/access to 401/403 and controlled dependency failure to 503. Retain internal safe trace references for diagnosis, but do not serialize raw provider exceptions to clients. # GET /health -> process status
# GET /ready -> readiness for declared fixture/live dependencies
# Inspect /openapi.json and correlate X-Request-ID with safe traces A readiness probe always returns ready despite an unavailable required index. A health probe calls the model, causing costs and false restarts during rate limits. Error bodies leak request headers or tokens. Test health under simulated dependency failure, readiness transitions, public error schemas and secret redaction. Check that every advertised route can be exercised with a known fixture.  Acceptance includes cheap probes, accurate readiness for the declared mode, typed OpenAPI and safe correlated errors. Fixture readiness states must not be mistaken for live-provider readiness. For SDETs, probe and API checks are deterministic operational contracts. They support deployment and recovery while quality metrics separately assess the model's task behavior.

title: Production architecture: queues, cache and idempotent effects
text:
A production AI path includes authentication, admission control, retrieval, provider work, validation and response delivery. Caches reduce repeated work, queues decouple long tasks, circuit breakers limit calls to failing dependencies and fallbacks preserve a smaller safe capability. Each mechanism changes failure behavior and needs a contract. Idempotency means repeating a request has the same intended effect as executing it once. A timeout is ambiguous: the remote system may have completed work even if the client received no response.  Key caches by tenant, permission scope, normalized request, prompt/model versions and index generation. Bound TTL and invalidate after permission or document changes. For side effects, persist an idempotency record before execution and return its existing result on duplicate requests. A circuit breaker moves closed to open after configured failures, then half-open for limited probes after cooldown. Queued work has an expiry and cancellation path. Fallback answers must indicate reduced capability and retain the same authorization rules. cache_key=('tenant-a','permissions-v2','prompt-v3','index-v4','question')
assert len(cache_key)==5 An open breaker routes to a backup provider with a different schema and the application treats arbitrary text as valid. A global cache returns another tenant's answer. A retry storm fills the queue faster than workers can drain it. Inject provider outage, slow storage, duplicate requests and permission revocation. Check bounded queue growth, consistent duplicate results, visible degraded mode and eventual recovery.  Architecture acceptance measures successful tasks under failure, not only normal throughput. Document which dependency failures cause abstention, fallback or rejection. SDETs should verify each transition with controlled faults and preserve traces for diagnosis. A retry mechanism is reliable only when it respects effect safety, capacity and deadlines.

title: Docker: reproducible images, non-root runtime and Compose
text:
An image packages filesystem layers and runtime metadata; a container is an isolated running instance. Dockerfile layer order affects dependency cache reuse. Copying dependency manifests before application source lets source-only changes avoid reinstalling dependencies. Containers improve reproducibility but do not automatically provide secure isolation, persistent data or correct service discovery. Secrets baked into layers can remain recoverable even if deleted later.  Use a pinned base image policy, locked dependencies, a non-root user and a narrow build context. Set an explicit working directory, install dependencies before copying source and launch uvicorn on the container interface. Provide health/readiness endpoints and graceful shutdown. Compose connects the API and optional Qdrant on an internal network with named persistent volumes. Keep provider secrets in runtime environment or secret mounts; exclude .env, caches and credentials with .dockerignore. Multi-stage builds can remove compilers from the final runtime. # Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
USER 10001
CMD ["uvicorn","app:app","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","8000"] The service listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container and is unreachable through a published port. A vector collection disappears after restart because no volume was attached. An image contains a copied .env. title: CI/CD: ordered checks, artifacts and release gates
text:
Continuous integration validates changes before they become release candidates. A useful pipeline installs locked dependencies, checks content and contracts, runs unit/integration tests, builds the app and executes representative browser and service tests. Continuous delivery packages a candidate after those gates; deployment publishes an approved artifact. An AI quality report belongs in the gate sequence. Producing HTML without using its exit verdict does not protect a release.  Use GitHub Actions jobs with explicit permissions, dependency caches and immutable artifacts. Run deterministic checks on every pull request. Live provider evaluations, when authorized and configured, use bounded datasets and protected secrets; forks must not receive those secrets. Upload failure traces and evaluation reports using always() while keeping the job failed. Build GitHub Pages with the repository base path and test route reloads before publishing. Link the artifact to code, dataset and prompt revisions. # CI command
python -m pytest local-labs
python local-labs/evals/runner.py --cases data/evaluation.json
npm run lint
npm test
npm run build A workflow appends || true to the evaluator and deploys despite hard-gate failures. A deployment rebuilds with different dependencies instead of publishing the tested artifact. A path filter skips tests when course JSON changes. Test that deliberate content corruption and failing cases produce nonzero checks. Review workflow permissions and ensure deployment depends on the complete validation job. Local evaluation returns a failing exit code for missing cases or violated invariants. SDETs should demonstrate a red build from a known regression, then a green build after the fix. text:

A path filter runs only for src/**/*.tsx and skips broken lesson JSON. Test the workflow logic with a known failing case and inspect that deployment cannot proceed. title: Cost engineering: useful-task budgets and routing
text:
AI cost includes input/output tokens, embedding/indexing work, retries, agent steps, evaluation and human review. Price per token is only one input to cost per accepted task. Smaller models, shorter context and caching help only if they preserve the required outcome. A routing policy sends simple cases to a low-cost path and escalates difficult or uncertain cases. Routing must be evaluated for false confidence, not merely average savings.  Set per-task and monthly budgets using dated provider rates. Track measured usage rather than estimating solely from characters. Cache authorized deterministic work and stable retrieval results, batch offline embedding jobs and reduce duplicate context. Use confidence thresholds calibrated on held-out cases to route accepted classifications, uncertain cases to stronger analysis and unsupported cases to humans. Bound agent steps and judge calls as part of the same budget. attempt_costs=[.003,.004,.002]
accepted=2

title: Enforce task budgets before hidden work grows

title: Performance tests: TTFT, tails and realistic workloads
text:
TTFT measures time to the first generated token; end-to-end latency measures completion; tokens per second describes generation rate. p50, p95 and p99 summarize latency distributions. Throughput counts completed tasks per unit time, while concurrency counts in-flight tasks. These quantities answer different capacity questions. Load tests need representative prompt length, retrieval work, output length, cache state and provider limits. Short fixture responses test service mechanics, not live-model generation capacity.  Use k6 or a controlled client with bounded arrivals, correlation IDs and separate latency measurements. Include cold and warm runs, slow streaming clients, rate limits and long context. Report offered load, accepted load, error rate and completed throughput. Avoid coordinated omission: a client that waits for each slow response before sending the next request hides overload. Set acceptance thresholds before testing and retain raw samples for tail analysis. import math
def percentile(values,p):
    v=sorted(values)
    return v[max(0,math.ceil(p/100*len(v))-1)] Average latency looks acceptable while a small group waits thirty seconds. text:

title: Reliability: controlled faults and graceful degradation
text:
Reliability is the ability to deliver an acceptable outcome despite dependency and input failures. AI failures include provider outage, rate limit, timeout, malformed result, hallucinated evidence, stale index, vector-store outage, broken tools, looping agents and context overflow. Not all failures should be retried. Graceful degradation preserves a smaller truthful capability, such as displaying retrieved evidence without a generated explanation. It must be visible to the user and obey the same permissions.  Define a failure matrix with detection, retryability, fallback, user response and recovery evidence. Use deadlines, bounded retries, circuit breakers, index freshness checks, schema validation and step budgets. Record final status as successful, degraded, rejected or failed. Inject one failure at a time in deterministic integration tests, then combine realistic correlated failures such as provider rate limits plus queue pressure. Ensure cancelled tasks release resources and duplicate requests cannot duplicate writes. fallback={'status':'degraded','answer':None,'evidence_ids':['D1']}
assert fallback['answer'] is None A fallback invents an explanation when retrieval is unavailable. A timeout handler retries indefinitely because each attempt resets the total deadline. A stale index passes health checks but returns deleted evidence. Assert visible degraded status, no unsupported claims, bounded attempts and eventual recovery. Simulate both empty evidence and contradictory evidence, because hallucination defenses depend on more than transport errors.  A reliability report shows each injected fault, observed status, trace and invariant outcome. Error budgets count user-visible failures over a specified window, with separate safety invariants that cannot be averaged away. SDETs should make fault cases executable release checks, not a list of possible risks. The system passes when it behaves predictably under the failures it claims to tolerate.

title: Turn the failure matrix into executable recovery contracts
text:
A failure matrix names each dependency fault, detection signal, allowed recovery and visible result. Provider timeouts, malformed responses, retrieval absence and unsafe tool requests require different handling. Retrying everything treats deterministic invalidity as if it were transient. Recovery must preserve the original trust boundary and budget. A fallback with broader access or unsupported claims turns a reliability mechanism into a security or quality regression.  Create one fixture per fault and assert final status, attempt limit, retained evidence and effects. The provider adapter uses an outer async deadline; the tool state machine stops repeated signatures; retrieval absence returns explicit abstention. For combined faults, test shared capacity and cancellation. Recheck permissions and approvals after a resumed task. Keep error categories stable in the public API while retaining safe internal diagnostic references. faults={'timeout':'unavailable','missing_context':'abstained','unsafe_write':'denied','loop':'stopped'}
assert len(set(faults.values()))==4 A malformed provider response is retried until the deadline but the public response still says success. A fallback copies another tenant's cached answer. A stopped agent's old partial draft is presented as a verified fix. Inspect actual state and effect counts, not just error wording. Test that resources are released and that the next healthy request can succeed after the fault is removed.  Acceptance records each fault, expected and observed outcome, trace and recovery evidence. A declared tolerance is supported only by an executed case. SDETs can run this suite without paid model calls by injecting the adapter/tool boundary. title: MLOps and LLMOps: versioned inputs and rollback
text:
A reproducible AI release links code, dataset, model, tokenizer, prompt, retrieval index, evaluation rubric and environment. MLOps manages training/serving artifacts; LLMOps adds prompt and provider configuration, retrieval and semantic evaluation. Both need experiment tracking and operational monitoring. title: Fine-tuning: data splits, LoRA and independent evaluation
text:
Prompting changes instructions, RAG supplies changing evidence, and fine-tuning changes model parameters for repeated task behavior. Fine-tuning is not a reliable way to maintain rapidly changing facts or enforce authorization. Start with a baseline and a measured failure pattern before paying training and maintenance costs. Supervised fine-tuning uses input/target examples. LoRA learns low-rank update matrices while keeping base weights frozen; PEFT is a broader family of parameter-efficient methods. These reduce trainable parameters, not the need for careful data and evaluation.  Create reviewed training examples with UNKNOWN and difficult classes, group related incidents to prevent leakage and reserve a held-out evaluation set. The optional local lab trains a tiny text classifier with torch; the PEFT example uses a configured public base checkpoint and LoRA adapter with explicit download/cost requirements. Compare against prompting and RAG baselines on accepted accuracy, calibration, safety, latency and total cost. Preserve source evidence outside weights. rank=4;input_dim=100;output_dim=80
full=input_dim*output_dim
lora=rank*(input_dim+output_dim)
assert lora<full Near-duplicate incidents appear in training and test, inflating accuracy. A fine-tuned model memorizes synthetic secret strings. Training loss falls while held-out performance declines, indicating overfitting. Test deduplication and grouped splits, evaluate rare classes and check that unsupported requests still abstain. Red-team the adapted model and do not infer security from a lower training loss.  Choose adaptation only if held-out gains justify operational complexity.
